en.title: Stories, Key Details & Daily Picture Sequences
en.summary: Locate exact Who/What/Where/When facts inside short A1 stories, read school posters, and sequence morning or weekend routines using First, Next, Then, and Finally.
goals: Scan every question word (Who = person, Where = place, When = time, How many = number).
Match picture timetable rows carefully before answering reading sign items.
Order three or four story events chronologically using signal words.

concepts.title: WH-Question Scanning
concepts.body: Underline key words before reading: WHO looks for a person's name, WHERE looks for a place, and WHEN looks for days or clock times.
concepts.formula: Who = Person | Where = Place | When = Time

concepts.body: Stories unfold step by step: First marks the start, Next/Then mark middle events, and Finally completes the ending.

cheat_sheet.title: Who vs Where
cheat_sheet.formula: Who asks a person; Where asks a location

cheat_sheet.title: Order Clue
cheat_sheet.formula: Look for First, Next, After that, Last

cheat_sheet.title: Schedule Check
cheat_sheet.formula: Compare AM morning vs PM afternoon carefully

cheat_sheet.title: Detail Proof
cheat_sheet.formula: Point straight to the exact line in the passage

traps: Do not pick an answer just because one word looks familiar; check ALL parts of the time and place.
If a schedule starts on Tuesday, do NOT select Monday just because Monday is a weekday.
Read EVERY step in the sequence strip before answering what happens 'just before' an event.

examples.title: Story Detail Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Every Thursday afternoon, Faisal walks to his grandfather's garden to water the lemon trees and feed three white rabbits.
Where does Faisal go on Thursday afternoon?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Match the question word 'Where' to the location named right after 'walks to'.

Step 1: Spot question word 'Where' -> place needed.

Step 2: Sentence says: walks to his grandfather's garden.

✅ Quick Check: His grandfather's garden.

examples.title: Zoo Gate Poster Reading
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Riyadh Bird Park Poster: Open 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Free entry for ages under 6. Please do not feed parrots bread.
According to the park poster, which visitor enters without paying a ticket?
options: A park bus driver at midnight
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Match the number constraint 'under 6' with candidate ages.

Step 1: Under 6 means younger than 6 years old.

Step 2: Age 5 is under 6.

✅ Quick Check: 5-year-old child.

examples.title: Counting Fact Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Salma packed two red apples, four date biscuits, and one bottle of milk for the picnic.
How many biscuits did Salma pack for the picnic?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Match the item asked ('biscuits') to its exact number word, not 'apples' or total items.

Step 1: Read carefully: two apples, FOUR date biscuits, one milk.

✅ Quick Check: Four.

ar.title: فهم القصص القصيرة والتفاصيل وتسلسل الأحداث
ar.summary: تحديد إجابات من وماذا وأين ومتى في القصص القصيرة، قراءة الملصقات المدرسية، وترتيب الأحداث باستخدام First وNext وFinally.
goals: تمييز أدوات الاستفهام الأساسية (من، أين، متى، كم) داخل الفقرة.
قراءة الجداول والملصقات بدقة قبل اختيار الإجابة.
ترتيب أحداث القصة زمنياً باستخدام كلمات التسلسل.

en.title: Tables, Signs, Simple Pronouns & Cause-and-Effect
en.summary: Extract data from simple classroom timetables, trace he/she/it/they back to earlier nouns, and answer 'Why' questions using 'because' clues.
goals: Link singular pronouns (he, she, it) and plural (they) directly to the preceding noun.
Spot 'because' or action-result links to identify why something happened.
Cross-read rows and columns in simple class schedules accurately.

concepts.title: Pronoun Matching Box
concepts.body: A pronoun stands in for an earlier noun: HE replaces one boy/man, SHE replaces one girl/woman, IT replaces one thing/animal, and THEY replaces two or more.
concepts.formula: He (1 boy) | She (1 girl) | It (1 object) | They (2+)

concepts.title: Why? Looking for Because
concepts.body: Cause tells WHY an event happened; effect tells WHAT happened as a result. Look for 'because' (points to cause) or 'so' (points to effect).

traps: Never match 'it' to plural nouns like 'books' or 'cats'; plural nouns use 'they'.
Don't confuse cause with effect—carrying an umbrella does NOT cause rain!
Double check whether a sign forbids an action ('Do NOT run') vs invites an action ('Join today').

examples.title: Pronoun Reference Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Reem painted a bright yellow kite yesterday. Then she hung it near the classroom window.
What does the word 'it' stand for?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: 'It' replaces one singular non-human object mentioned in sentence 1.

Step 1: Reem uses 'she'; kite is the singular object hung up.

✅ Quick Check: the yellow kite.

examples.title: Cause and Effect Why
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Tariq wore his thick wool coat this morning because a cold north wind was blowing across town.
Why did Tariq put on his thick wool coat?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Read right after 'because' to uncover the reason.

Step 1: Target sentence says '...because a cold north wind was blowing'.

✅ Quick Check: Cold wind.

examples.title: Plural Pronoun Tracking
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Two friendly camels stood beside the tent. They drank cool water from a large stone bowl.
Who or what does 'They' refer to?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: 'They' refers to a plural noun (> 1).

Step 1: Only 'Two friendly camels' is plural in sentence 1.

✅ Quick Check: The two camels.

examples.title: تحديد الاسم العائد عليه الضمير
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Reem painted a bright yellow kite yesterday. Then she hung it near the classroom window.
إلى ماذا يشير الضمير it في الجملة الثانية؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: يعود الضمير it على الشيء المفرد غير العاقل المذكور في الجملة الأولى.

الخطوة 1: ريم يعود عليها she، بينما الطائرة الورقية يعود عليها it.

✅ التحقق من الحل: الطائرة الورقية الصفراء.

Tariq wore his thick wool coat this morning because a cold north wind was blowing across town.
لماذا ارتدى طارق معطفه الصوفي السميك؟

examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Two friendly camels stood beside the tent. They drank cool water from a large stone bowl.
إلى من يشير الضمير They؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الضمير They يعود دائماً على اسم جمع، والجمع الوحيد هو الجملان.

الخطوة 1: تدل كلمة Two camels على اثنين، لذا استُخدم They.

✅ التحقق من الحل: الجملان.

en.title: Main Idea, Dialogue Feelings, Politeness & Fact vs. Opinion
en.summary: Find what a short passage is mostly about (Main Idea), read feelings and polite dialogue replies (Thank you / Excuse me), and tell true verifiable facts apart from personal opinions.
goals: Spot the umbrella sentence that covers ALL details in a paragraph rather than one small detail.
Match dialogue greetings, apologies, and polite requests to everyday school situations.
Identify subjective opinion words ('best', 'tastiest', 'fun') vs. verifiable objective facts.

concepts.title: Main Idea vs. Small Detail
concepts.body: Think of Main Idea as the table top and supporting details as the four table legs holding it up.
concepts.formula: Main Idea = Whole Umbrella | Detail = One Example

concepts.title: Polite Dialogue & Feelings
concepts.body: Match feelings to clues ('smiles wide' = glad; 'drops ice cream' = sad) and pick kind replies like 'May I borrow...', 'I am sorry', and 'You are welcome'.
concepts.formula: Help -> Thank you -> You are welcome

concepts.title: Facts vs. Opinions
concepts.body: A FACT can be measured or checked ('Jeddah sits beside the Red Sea'); an OPINION shares feelings ('Winter is the best season').
concepts.formula: Fact = Proven True | Opinion = Feeling / Best / Favorite

cheat_sheet.title: Main Idea Test
cheat_sheet.formula: Must cover sentences 1, 2, AND 3 together

cheat_sheet.title: Opinion Adjectives
cheat_sheet.formula: Watch for: favorite, best, boring, prettiest, yummy

cheat_sheet.title: Warning Sign
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Keep off grass' protects park lawns

cheat_sheet.title: Feeling Clues
cheat_sheet.formula: Smiled & jumped -> proud / excited

traps: A detail mentioned in ONLY ONE sentence is too narrow to be the Main Idea.
'Everyone likes honey' sounds confident, yet 'likes' makes it an OPINION/claim, not a measurable fact.
When someone says 'I am sorry I dropped your pencil', the polite reply is 'That is okay!'.

examples.title: Main Idea Umbrella Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Before school, Omar brushes his teeth. After gym, he washes his hands with soap. At night, he takes a warm bath and goes to bed early.
What is the BEST main idea for all three sentences?
options: Omar stays up reading all night
Omar follows healthy clean habits daily
Omar forgets where his toothbrush sits
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Combine tooth brushing, hand washing, and early sleeping under one common theme.

Step 1: Tooth brushing + hand washing + bath + sleep = daily healthy habits.

✅ Quick Check: Healthy clean habits.

examples.title: Polite Reply Matching
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Teacher Ms. Huda hands Layla a sharpened green pencil. Layla smiles and says, 'Thank you very much!'
What should Ms. Huda say next?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Standard polite response to 'Thank you' is 'You are welcome'.

Step 1: 'Thank you' -> reply 'You are welcome'.

✅ Quick Check: You are welcome.

examples.title: Fact vs. Opinion Choice
examples.question: Walkthrough: Which sentence states a scientific FACT that everyone can check, rather than a personal opinion?
options: Water freezes into solid ice at zero degrees Celsius
Green backpacks look cooler than blue ones
Strawberry ice cream tastes better than vanilla
Fridays are much more exciting than Mondays
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Look for measurable truth without preference adjectives ('better', 'cooler', 'more exciting').

Step 1: Freezing point 0 C is testable everywhere; taste/colors are opinions.

✅ Quick Check: Water freezes at 0 C.

examples.title: Reading Emotion Clues
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Sami lost his new soccer ball behind the wall, sat on the grass with tears in his eyes, and looked down quietly.
How does Sami most likely feel?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Tears and sitting quietly after losing a toy reveal sadness.

Step 1: Lost ball + tears -> sad and upset.

✅ Quick Check: Sad and upset.

ar.title: الفكرة الرئيسة ومشاعر الشخصيات والتهذيب والحقيقة والرأي
ar.summary: تحديد الفكرة الرئيسة للفقرة القصيرة، استنتاج مشاعر الشخصيات وأسلوب الرد المهذب، والتمييز بين الحقيقة العلمية والرأي الشخصي.
goals: اختيار الفكرة الشاملة التي تغطي كامل الفقرة لا تفصيلاً صغيراً واحداً.
اختيار العبارة المهذبة المناسبة لكل موقف في الحوار.
التمييز بين الرأي الشخصي والحقيقة القابلة للتحقق.

concepts.title: الفكرة الرئيسة مقابل التفاصيل
concepts.body: الفكرة الرئيسة هي العنوان الكبير الذي يشمل كل الجمل، بينما التفاصيل هي الأمثلة الصغيرة الداعمة له.

concepts.title: أدب الحوار ومشاعر المتحدث
concepts.body: اربط التصرف بالشعور المناسب واختر عبارات اللباقة مثل Excuse me وThank you وYou are welcome.
concepts.formula:
ردود الحوار المهذبة:
$\text{شكر} \to \text{عفواً (You are welcome)}$

examples.title: اختيار الفكرة الرئيسة الشاملة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Before school, Omar brushes his teeth. After gym, he washes his hands with soap. At night, he takes a warm bath and goes to bed early.
ما أفضل فكرة رئيسة تشمل الجمل الثلاث كلها؟
options: يتبع عمر عادات صحية ونظافة يومية
examples.explanation:

الخطوة 1: جميع الجمل تصف النظافة والعادات الصحية لعمر.

✅ التحقق من الحل: عادات صحية يومية.

en.title: High-Frequency Words, Synonyms, Antonyms & Category Groups
en.summary: Build A1 sight vocabulary around school/home/weather, solve fill-in-the-blank context sentences, pair everyday synonyms and opposites, and spot the odd word out of a category.
goals: Spot synonym pairs ('happy / glad', 'big / large', 'fast / quick') and opposites ('tall / short', 'open / close').
Group words by family (fruits, animals, colors, seasons, school tools) to eliminate an odd item.
Read the whole sentence around a blank before picking the best vocabulary match.

concepts.title: Synonyms & Antonyms Pairs
concepts.body: Synonyms share nearly the same meaning (happy = glad, start = begin). Antonyms carry opposite meanings (hot vs. cold, early vs. late).
concepts.formula: Synonyms ($=$): big / large | Antonyms ($\neq$): big / tiny

concepts.body: Check what three words share (four seasons, three tools, or three fruits) so the fourth unrelated word stands out immediately.

concepts.title: Word Parts Introduction
concepts.body: Adding small endings changes word clues: '-s/-es' makes plural, '-ful' adds 'full of' (careful = full of care), and 'un-' means 'not' (unhappy = not happy).
concepts.formula: un + happy = not happy | help + ful = helpful

cheat_sheet.formula: Read carefully: does item ask SAME or OPPOSITE?

cheat_sheet.title: Prefix un-
cheat_sheet.formula: 'un-' flips meaning to the opposite (unfair = not fair)

cheat_sheet.title: Odd Word Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: Three items belong together; one belongs elsewhere

cheat_sheet.title: Blank Fit Check
cheat_sheet.formula: Read the completed sentence aloud mentally

traps: A frequent mistake on synonym vs. antonym questions is picking the opposite when the question asks for SAME meaning!
Read 'desert' (dry sandy land) vs 'dessert' (sweet treat after dinner) carefully.
If three words are verbs (run, jump, swim) and one is a noun (table), 'table' is the odd word out.

examples.title: Opposite Meaning Match
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
The library floor stays completely QUIET during reading time, unlike the loud playground outside.
Which word means the OPPOSITE of 'quiet'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Opposite of peaceful silence is loud noise.

Step 1: Silent, calm, soft are close to quiet; noisy/loud is the opposite.

✅ Quick Check: noisy / loud.

ar.title: المفردات الأساسية والمترادفات والأضداد والتصنيف
ar.summary: إتقان المفردات اليومية، إكمال الفراغ من سياق الجملة، ربط المترادفات والأضداد، واستخراج الكلمة المختلفة عن المجموعة.
goals: ربط المترادفات والأضداد الشائعة بدقة.
تصنيف الكلمات حسب الفئة لاستبعاد الكلمة الغريبة.
قراءة الجملة كاملة قبل اختيار الكلمة المكملة للفراغ.

concepts.title: المترادفات والأضداد الشائعة
concepts.body: المترادفات تتقارب في المعنى مثل كبير/ضخم، والأضداد تتعاكس مثل ساخن/بارد ومبكر/متأخر.

examples.title: إيجاد الضد الصحيح
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
The library floor stays completely QUIET during reading time, unlike the loud playground outside.
أي كلمة تعني عكس كلمة quiet (هادئ)؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عكس الهدوء هو الضجيج والصوت المرتفع.

الخطوة 1: silent وcalm ترادف الهدوء، أما noisy/loud فهي الضد.

✅ التحقق من الحل: صاخب.

examples.question: تطبيق محلول: انظر لبطاقة الكلمات: أي كلمة لا تنتمي إلى المجموعة؟
examples.explanation:

examples.title: تفسير السابقة un-
examples.question: تطبيق محلول: انظر لبطاقة تركيب الكلمة: UN- + KIND. ما معنى كلمة unkind؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: البادئة un- تدل على النفي، فيصبح المعنى غير لطيف.

الخطوة 1: un- تعني غير، إذن unkind تعني غير لطيف.

✅ التحقق من الحل: غير لطيف.

en.title: Everyday Prepositions, Compound Words & Picture Clues
en.summary: Distinguish spatial prepositions (in, on, under, beside, between), split compound nouns into two base words (sun + flower, rain + bow), and read real-world label context clues.
goals: Use accurate place prepositions (between 2 objects vs. inside a box vs. under a table).
Recognize compound words formed by joining two smaller nouns.
Decode unfamiliar A1 words using surrounding action verbs and setting clues.

concepts.title: Place Prepositions Guide
concepts.body: Use IN inside an enclosed space, ON resting atop a surface, UNDER directly beneath, BESIDE next to, and BETWEEN with two flanking neighbors.

cheat_sheet.title: Between Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: Requires TWO items on either side (A and B)

cheat_sheet.title: Compound Check
cheat_sheet.formula: Both halves must stand as real English words

cheat_sheet.title: On vs Over
cheat_sheet.formula: 'On' touches surface; 'under' sits below

cheat_sheet.title: Context First
cheat_sheet.formula: Verify part of speech (noun/verb/adjective)

traps: Never pick 'between' when only one object is named; say 'beside' or 'next to' instead.
'Unhappy' is NOT a compound word because 'un-' is a prefix, not a standalone word like 'sun' or 'book'.

examples.title: Compound Noun Meaning
examples.question: Walkthrough: Look at the word card 'book + shelf'. Where would you look to find a 'bookshelf'?
options: holding reading books in a room

examples.title: Spatial Preposition Between
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
In our classroom shelf, the green globe sits on the left, the red atlas sits on the right, and a silver clock sits in the middle of the two.
Which preposition completes: 'The silver clock is ____ the globe and the atlas'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Middle position flanked by two objects takes 'between ... and ...'.

Step 1: Notice 'and' pairing two items: globe AND atlas -> between.

✅ Quick Check: between.

examples.title: Word Splitting Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Zaid carried a colorful BACKPACK filled with science notebooks and markers.
Which two smaller words form the compound word 'backpack'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Split between two real English words that explain carrying a pack on your back.

Step 1: 'back' (part of body) + 'pack' (bundle carried) -> backpack.

✅ Quick Check: back + pack.

ar.title: حروف الجر المكانية والكلمات المركبة وسياق الصورة
ar.summary: إتقان حروف الجر المكانية، تحليل الكلمات المركبة إلى جزأيها، وفهم المفردات من سياق اللوحات اليومية.

examples.explanation:

In our classroom shelf, the green globe sits on the left, the red atlas sits on the right, and a silver clock sits in the middle of the two.

examples.explanation:

examples.question:

Before boarding the plane at King Khalid Airport, Amal showed her boarding ____ to the smiling gate agent.
ما الكلمة المناسبة لإكمال سياق السفر في المطار؟

examples.title: تحليل الكلمة المركبة إلى جزأين
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Zaid carried a colorful BACKPACK filled with science notebooks and markers.
أي كلمتين تشكلان الكلمة المركبة backpack؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نقسم الكلمة إلى كلمتين مستقلتين تعطيان المعنى: حقيبة تُحمل على الظهر.

الخطوة 1: back (ظهر) + pack (حزمة/حقيبة).

✅ التحقق من الحل: back + pack.

en.title: To Be, Present Simple, Plurals, Articles & Punctuation
en.summary: Conjugate am/is/are and have/has accurately, add third-person singular -s, pick a/an/the and irregular plurals (children/feet/mice), and fix capitalization and end punctuation.
goals: Match subjects rigorously: I am, he/she/it IS, you/we/they ARE.
Pick 'an' strictly before vowel SOUNDS (an apple, an hour) and 'a' before consonant sounds.
Capitalize the first word, names (Riyadh, Monday, Sara), and 'I', and end questions with '?'.

concepts.title: Verb To Be & Have Agreement
concepts.body: Singular nouns (Sara, the cat) take IS / HAS / PLAYS (-s). Plural subjects (cats, we, you, they) take ARE / HAVE / PLAY (base form).
concepts.formula: He/She/It $\to$ is / has / eats | They/We $\to$ are / have / eat
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Subject-Verb Match" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Subject-Verb Match</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Subject-Verb Match</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">I</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">am / have / read</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">He / She / It</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">is / has / reads</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">We / You / They</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">are / have / read</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">There is vs are</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">1 book vs 3 books</text></svg>

concepts.title: A / An & Common Plurals
concepts.body: Use 'an' before vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u: an orange, an umbrella). Learn irregular plurals: child -> children, foot -> feet, mouse -> mice, tooth -> teeth.

concepts.title: Present Tense on the Timeline
concepts.body: Use Simple Present for daily habits and facts ('Every morning, the bus arrives at 7:00') and Present Continuous ('Right now, she is writing') for happening-now actions.

cheat_sheet.title: Hidden 'I'
cheat_sheet.formula: Pronoun 'I' is ALWAYS capital even mid-sentence

cheat_sheet.title: Sound Not Letter
cheat_sheet.formula: Use 'a university' (y-sound), 'an orange'

cheat_sheet.title: Plural Verb Trap
cheat_sheet.formula: Kids RUN fast (no -s on verb with plural subject!)

cheat_sheet.title: Question Mark ?
cheat_sheet.formula: Sentences starting Who/What/Do/Is end with '?'

traps: NEVER add '-s' to an English plural verb! Compare: 'One bird sings' vs. 'Two birds sing'.
Do not write 'childs' or 'foots'—always check for irregular plural nouns.
Remember every sentence needs a capital starter AND an end mark (. ? !).

examples.title: Subject-Verb Match
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
My little sister Huda ____ two pet goldfish in a round glass bowl.
Which verb form correctly fills the blank?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: 'My little sister Huda' is one third-person singular girl -> uses 'has'.

Step 1: Count subject: 1 person (Huda = she) -> has.

✅ Quick Check: has.

examples.title: Article Before Vowel Sound
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Uncle Khalid peeled ____ sweet orange after walking home from the mosque.
Choose the correct article before 'sweet' or check carefully: notice 'sweet' starts with 's'!
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Look at the VERY NEXT word right after the blank ('sweet'), NOT 'orange'!

Step 1: The word directly following the blank is 'sweet' (starts with consonant /s/).

Step 2: Say 'a sweet orange' (whereas without 'sweet', it would be 'an orange').

✅ Quick Check: a.

examples.title: Irregular Noun Plural
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Five young ____ built a tall sandcastle beside the Red Sea shore.
Which plural noun fits after 'Five'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Child has the irregular plural 'children' (never add -s at the end).

Step 1: Five requires plural -> children.

✅ Quick Check: children.

examples.title: Sentence Capitalization & Mark
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Draft line to fix: "when does the jeddah train leave"
Which editing rule corrects EVERY error in the draft sentence?
options: Capitalize 'When', capitalize 'Jeddah', and finish with a question mark (?)
Keep all letters lowercase and finish with a comma (,)
Capitalize only 'train' and finish with a period (.)
Remove 'When' and finish with an exclamation mark (!)
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Check all three rules: Capital 'W', Capital proper city 'Jeddah', and '?' for 'When...'.

Step 1: Rule 1: Start 'When' capital; Rule 2: 'Jeddah' proper city; Rule 3: '?' question mark.

✅ Quick Check: When does the Jeddah train leave?

ar.title: أفعال الكينونة والمضارع البسيط والجمع وأدوات التعريف والترقيم
ar.summary: تصريف am/is/are وhave/has، إضافة -s للمفرد الغائب، استخدام a/an والجمع الشاذ، وضبط الحروف الكبيرة وعلامات الترقيم.
goals: مطابقة الفاعل مع الفعل المساعد (is للمفرد، are للجمع، am لـ I).
اختيار a قبل الأصوات الساكنة وan قبل الأصوات المتحركة.
بدء الجملة وأسماء الأعلام والضمير I بحرف كبير ووضع نقطة أو علامة استفهام.

concepts.title: توافق الفعل المساعد مع الفاعل
concepts.body: الفاعل المفرد الغائب يأخذ is/has وفعل ينتهي بـ s، بينما الجمع وyou وI تأخذ الفعل الأساسي وare/have.
concepts.formula:
جدول التوافق:
$\text{مفرد غائب} \to \text{is / has / +s} \mid \text{جمع} \to \text{are / have}$
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Subject-Verb Match" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Subject-Verb Match</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Subject-Verb Match</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">I</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">am / have / read</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">He / She / It</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">is / has / reads</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">We / You / They</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">are / have / read</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">There is vs are</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">1 book vs 3 books</text></svg>

concepts.body: نضع an قبل الكلمات المبدوءة بصوت متحرك، ونحفظ الجموع الشاذة مثل children وfeet وteeth.

cheat_sheet.formula: الجملة المبدوءة بأداة سؤال تنتهي بعلامة ?

traps: لا نضيف -s للفعل مع الفاعل الجمع أبداً: الطائر يغرد (sings) والطيور تغرد (sing).
احذر جمع الكلمات الشاذة بالـ s مثل childs؛ الجمع الصحيح children.

examples.title: توافق الفعل مع الفاعل المفرد والجمع
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
My little sister Huda ____ two pet goldfish in a round glass bowl.
أي صيغة فعل تكمل الجملة بشكل صحيح؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الفاعل 'أختي الصغيرة هدى' اسم مفرد مؤنث غائب، لذا يأخذ الفعل has.

الخطوة 1: المفرد الغائب يأخذ has بدلاً من have.

✅ التحقق من الحل: has.

examples.title: اختيار أداة التنكير المناسبة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Uncle Khalid peeled ____ sweet orange after walking home from the mosque.
اختر أداة التنكير الصحيحة قبل عبارة sweet orange (انتبه لصوت كلمة sweet):
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: ننظر دائماً للحرف الصوتي لأول كلمة بعد الفراغ مباشرة وهي sweet لا orange.

الخطوة 1: تبدأ sweet بصوت ساكن /s/ فتأخذ الأداة a.

✅ التحقق من الحل: a.

examples.title: الجمع الشاذ لـ foot وchild
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Five young ____ built a tall sandcastle beside the Red Sea shore.
ما صيغة الجمع الصحيحة بعد العدد Five؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: جمع الكلمة الشاذة child هو children دون إضافة s.

en.title: Informational Texts, Timetables, Inference & Cause-Effect
en.summary: Extract multi-step facts from science and geography texts, cross-read multi-column event timetables with constraints, make evidence-based inferences, and connect complex causes to outcomes.
goals: Eliminate distractors that swap numbers, days, or conditions from neighboring table rows.
Combine explicit text clues with background logic to draw warranted A2 inferences.
Distinguish direct causes from chronological coincidences in informational passages.

concepts.title: Two-Constraint Table Reading
concepts.body: Check EVERY condition requested (e.g., BOTH cost <= 5 SAR AND arriving before 4 PM) across each table row instead of stopping at the first match.

concepts.title: Evidence-Based Inference Formula
concepts.body: Authors do not always state feelings or motives directly. Combine what the character DOES in the text with real-world reasoning to infer accurately.
concepts.formula: Text Clue + Logical Link = Valid Inference

cheat_sheet.title: Dual Filter Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: Test EVERY option against both time and budget rules

cheat_sheet.title: Inference Guard
cheat_sheet.formula: Never pick extreme words like 'never/always/all' unless stated

cheat_sheet.title: Cause Words
cheat_sheet.formula: since, because, as a result, therefore, so that

cheat_sheet.title: Exact Pronoun
cheat_sheet.formula: Re-read substituting candidate noun into the sentence

traps: Stopping after checking only the first rule in a timetable question is the #1 reason students miss Level 2 items.
An inference must be strongly supported—not merely 'possible' if ungrounded in clues.

examples.title: Two-Constraint Schedule Choice
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Students in Abha have a budget of 12 SAR and must start their visit before noon (12:00 PM).
Checking the Museum Schedule card, which activity satisfies BOTH rules?

examples.title: Logical Inference From Actions
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Before locking the classroom door, Nadia checked all four window latches, unplugged the projector, and placed her potted fern inside the shaded hallway.
Why did Nadia move her potted fern and lock the windows?
options: Windows were broken by strong hail
The school was closing for an extended break or holiday
She planned to repaint every desk immediately
The fern grew faster in total darkness
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Unplugging electronics + moving plants out of locked sunny rooms signals nobody returns for several days.

Step 1: Four careful closing steps together point to an extended school break.

✅ Quick Check: Extended school break.

examples.title: Cross-Sentence Pronoun Link
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Modern windmills catch steady mountain breezes cleanly. Because they turn slow blades, engineers mount them high along windy ridges.
What does 'them' refer to in the second sentence?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Ask what object engineers mount high up on ridges.

Step 1: Engineers cannot mount breezes or themselves; they mount 'modern windmills'.

✅ Quick Check: modern windmills.

ar.title: نصوص المعلومات والجداول الزمنية والاستنتاج والسبب والنتيجة
ar.summary: استخراج المعلومات الدقيقة من نصوص العلوم والجغرافيا، قراءة جداول المواعيد متعددة القيود، بناء الاستنتاج المنطقي، وربط الأسباب بالنتائج.
goals: استبعاد الخيارات التي تخلط أرقام الصفوف المجاورة في الجداول.
ربط القرائن الصريحة بالمنطق للوصول إلى استنتاج سليم.
التفريق بين العلاقة السببية والتتابع الزمني فقط.

concepts.title: قراءة الجداول ذات الشرطين
concepts.body: تحقق من جميع الشروط معاً (مثل التكلفة الأقل والوقت المحدد) في كل صف قبل اختيار الإجابة.
concepts.formula:

en.title: Summarizing Passages, Dialogues & Multi-Paragraph Details
en.summary: Synthesize two-paragraph articles accurately, distinguish explicit evidence from unsupported leaps in dialogue comprehension, and answer sequence-based reading questions.
goals: Select balanced summaries covering beginning, middle, and conclusion without adding invented claims.
Trace multi-speaker agreements (who brings what, which time changed) inside dialogue exchanges.
Compare paired short notes (email + calendar update) to spot final updated arrangements.

concepts.title: Balanced Summary Rules
concepts.body: A good summary combines the main ideas of ALL paragraphs in neutral words, omits tiny examples, and adds zero outside opinions.
concepts.formula: Para 1 Idea + Para 2 Idea = Balanced Summary

concepts.body: Speakers often suggest a first time ('Meet at 4:00?'), then change plans ('Wait—let's make it 4:30 instead'). Always track the FINAL confirmed plan!

examples.title: Final Dialogue Agreement
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Rami texted: 'Shall we practice robotics at 4:00 PM?' Khalid replied: 'My dentist appointment ends at 4:15, so let's start at 4:30 PM instead in Lab B.'
At what time and place will the boys meet?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Follow Khalid's correction ('instead') rather than Rami's initial proposal.

Step 1: 4:00 PM was rejected for dentist visit -> final confirmed slot = 4:30 PM in Lab B.

✅ Quick Check: 4:30 PM in Lab B.

examples.title: Two-Paragraph Summary Choice
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Para 1: Plastic bags blow easily into Arabian Gulf waters, where sea turtles mistake them for jellyfish. Para 2: Youth volunteer teams in Jubail now sort beach plastic every Saturday and use cloth bags in shops.
Which sentence best summarizes BOTH paragraphs?
options: Sea turtles love eating blue jellyfish near sandy dunes
Shops in Jubail stopped selling Saturday groceries
Plastic bags melt immediately when hitting cold water
Plastic pollution harms sea turtles, so coastal volunteers work to collect waste and switch to cloth bags
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Join Para 1 problem (harm to sea turtles) + Para 2 action (cleanup & cloth bags).

Step 1: Covers harm AND youth solution evenly without distortion.

✅ Quick Check: Balanced two-part summary.

examples.title: Supporting Detail Exclusion
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
During spring, Al-Ahsa oasis date farmers trim dry fronds and guide spring irrigation channels carefully around young palm shoots.
Which claim is NOT supported anywhere in the passage?
options: Dry palm fronds get trimmed in spring
Irrigation water reaches palm roots through channels
Young palm shoots grow in Al-Ahsa
Farmers harvest all dates using winter helicopters
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Verify each option directly word-for-word against the short passage.

Step 1: Spring trimming, irrigation channels, Al-Ahsa young palms match; helicopters are fabricated.

✅ Quick Check: Winter helicopters.

goals: اختيار الملخص المتوازن الذي يضم فكرتي الفقرتين دون زيادة معلومات من خارج النص.

المقارنة بين رسالة قصيرة وتحديث جدول لتحديد القرار النهائي.

examples.title: استخراج الاتفاق النهائي في الحوار
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Rami texted: 'Shall we practice robotics at 4:00 PM?' Khalid replied: 'My dentist appointment ends at 4:15, so let's start at 4:30 PM instead in Lab B.'
في أي وقت ومكان سيلتقي الطالبان؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نعتمد الموعد النهائي بعد عبارة التعديل instead لا الاقتراح المرفوض.

en.title: Author's Purpose (PIE), Tone, Fact vs. Opinion & Transition Words
en.summary: Classify Persuade/Inform/Entertain purposes, identify warm/urgent/formal writer tone, distinguish verified facts from value judgments, and bridge contrasting clauses using however/although/moreover.
goals: Apply the P-I-E test: Persuade (convince you), Inform (explain facts/steps), Entertain (story/humor).
Select contrasting connectors ('however', 'although') vs. additive ('moreover', 'in addition') vs. result ('therefore').
Recognize bias or persuasive opinion language inside school announcements and ads.

concepts.title: P-I-E Purpose Model
concepts.body: Authors write to PERSUADE (buy/join/agree with reasons), INFORM (teach real science, history, instructions), or ENTERTAIN (tell fun adventures).
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Author Purpose Key" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Author Purpose Key</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Author Purpose Key</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Persuade</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Should, must, join now!</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Inform</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Data tables, how-to steps, dates</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Entertain</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Characters, plot, humor</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Warn</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Do not touch; caution rules</text></svg>

concepts.body: Match logical relationship first: Contrast ('however', 'although', 'yet'), Addition ('moreover', 'also'), and Result ('therefore', 'so').
concepts.formula: Contrast: however | Add: moreover | Result: therefore

cheat_sheet.title: PIE Clues
cheat_sheet.formula: 'You should...' = Persuade; 'First, fold...' = Inform

cheat_sheet.title: Contrast Check
cheat_sheet.formula: Good weather + stayed inside -> needs 'however/yet'

cheat_sheet.title: Additive Clue
cheat_sheet.formula: Sentence 2 gives a 2nd supporting point -> 'moreover'

cheat_sheet.title: Result Clue
cheat_sheet.formula: Rain poured -> 'therefore', matches moved inside

traps: Never pick 'Entertain' for a clean museum instruction poster just because the topic sounds interesting!
'Although' opens one clause and needs a comma—NEVER pair 'although' AND 'but' together in the same sentence.

examples.title: Author Purpose Identification
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Join our school recycling brigade every Wednesday! Bringing just five empty water bottles each week saves landfill space and keeps our courtyard spotless.
What is the author's PRIMARY purpose in writing this message?
options: To entertain readers with a fictional mystery story
To warn hikers about mountain windstorms
To persuade students to participate in weekly recycling
To instruct engineers how to melt glass in factories
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Spot imperative 'Join' and benefits aimed at changing reader behavior -> Persuade.

Step 1: Calls reader to action ('Join') and lists motivating benefits.

✅ Quick Check: Persuade students.

examples.title: Contrast Connector Choice
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
The desert trail looked flat from the hilltop; ____, hikers soon discovered deep rocky gullies hidden below.

Step 1: Opposite reality vs appearance demands contrast word -> however.

✅ Quick Check: however.

examples.title: Fact vs. Judgment Audit
examples.question: Walkthrough: Which sentence from a Red Sea brochure contains an OPINION rather than an objective fact?
options: Summer seawater temperatures near the reef stay near 29 C
Coral reefs support over two hundred local fish species
Sunset boat rides off Yanbu offer the most unforgettable evening on Earth
Yanbu Port lies along the western Red Sea coast
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Spot subjective praise ('most unforgettable') that cannot be measured by instruments.

Step 1: Locations, 29 C, and species counts are measurable facts; 'most unforgettable' is a personal rating.

✅ Quick Check: Sunset rides offer...

examples.title: Additive Connector Logic
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Solar streetlamps lower city electricity bills every night. ____, they keep working smoothly during summer grid repairs.
Which transition adds a second supporting benefit?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Sentence 2 gives another positive advantage on the SAME side as Sentence 1.

Step 1: Advantage 1 (lower bills) + Advantage 2 (keep working) -> additive connector Moreover.

✅ Quick Check: Moreover.

examples.title: تحديد الغرض الأساسي للكاتب
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Join our school recycling brigade every Wednesday! Bringing just five empty water bottles each week saves landfill space and keeps our courtyard spotless.
ما الغرض الرئيس من كتابة هذه الرسالة؟
options: إقناع الطلاب بالمشاركة في إعادة التدوير الأسبوعية
شرح طريقة صهر الزجاج في المصانع
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: فعل الأمر 'انضم' مع ذكر الفوائد التحفيزية يثبت أن الغرض هو الإقناع.

الخطوة 1: نداء المشاركة المباشر يدل على غرض الإقناع.

✅ التحقق من الحل: إقناع الطلاب بالمشاركة.

examples.title: اختيار أداة التضاد المناسبة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
The desert trail looked flat from the hilltop; ____, hikers soon discovered deep rocky gullies hidden below.
أي أداة ربط تكمل المعنى التضادي بين الجملتين؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: المعنى الثاني (أودية صخرية عميقة) يناقض المظهر الأول (يبدو منبسطاً)، لذا نستخدم أداة التضاد.

الخطوة 1: كلمة however تربط فكرتين متقابلتين.

✅ التحقق من الحل: however.

examples.title: التمييز بين التقرير الموضوعي والرأي
examples.question: تطبيق محلول: أي جملة من كتيب البحر الأحمر تعبّر عن رأي لا حقيقة موضوعية؟
options: تبلغ حرارة المياه قرب الشعاب نحو 29 درجة
تحتضن الشعاب المرجانية أكثر من مئتي نوع من الأسماك
تقدم رحلات الغروب في ينبع أجمل أمسية لا تُنسى على وجه الأرض
يقع ميناء ينبع على الساحل الغربي للبحر الأحمر
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تعبير 'الأجمل والأكثر إمتاعاً على وجه الأرض' تقييم ذاتي غير قابل للقياس.

الخطوة 1: الأرقام والمواقع حقائق، أما وصف الرحلة بأجمل أمسية فرأي.

✅ التحقق من الحل: رحلات الغروب أجمل أمسية.

examples.title: استخدام أداة الإضافة moreover
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Solar streetlamps lower city electricity bills every night. ____, they keep working smoothly during summer grid repairs.
أي أداة ربط تضيف ميزة إضافية ثانية للمصابيح الشمسية؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الجملة الثانية تضيف فائدة ثانية في نفس الاتجاه الإيجابي للأولى، لذا نختار Moreover.

الخطوة 1: أدوات الإضافة تُستخدم لدعم الفكرة بميزة أخرى.

✅ التحقق من الحل: Moreover.

en.title: Prefix/Suffix Morphology & Context Definition Clues
en.summary: Decode unfamiliar A2 words via prefixes (un-, re-, pre-, dis-, mis-) and suffixes (-ful, -less, -er, -ly, -able), and use inline contrast, example, or definition clues inside sentences.
goals: Split long words into Prefix + Root + Suffix to predict meaning systematically.
Contrast '-ful' (full of) vs. '-less' (without) and 're-' (again) vs. 'pre-' (before).
Use inline signals ('such as', 'unlike', dashes, commas) to define unknown words.

concepts.title: Prefix Meaning Grid
concepts.body: Prefixes sit BEFORE roots: un-/dis- = NOT or opposite, re- = AGAIN, pre- = BEFORE, mis- = WRONGLY.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 155" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Prefix + Root + Suffix" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Prefix + Root + Suffix</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="139" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Prefix + Root + Suffix</text><rect x="24" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="70" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#dc2626">Prefix</text><text x="70" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">re-</text><rect x="134" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="180" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Root</text><text x="180" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">use</text><rect x="244" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="290" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#16a34a">Suffix</text><text x="290" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">-able</text><text x="180" y="129" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Meaning: can use again</text></svg>

concepts.title: Suffixes Change Word Class
concepts.body: Suffixes attach AFTER roots: -er = person/tool (teacher), -ly = adverb (quickly), -able = can be (washable), -less = without (careless).
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 155" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Suffix Function" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Suffix Function</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="139" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Suffix Function</text><rect x="24" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="70" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#dc2626">Prefix</text><text x="70" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">—</text><rect x="134" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="180" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Root</text><text x="180" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">care</text><rect x="244" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="290" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#16a34a">Suffix</text><text x="290" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">-less</text><text x="180" y="129" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Meaning: without care</text></svg>

concepts.title: Four Context Clue Signals
concepts.body: Authors leave helpful clues: Definition commas ('arid, or dry, climate'), Examples ('reptiles such as lizards'), Contrast ('generous unlike selfish'), and Logic.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-1.3 0 372.6 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Context Clue Signals" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:373px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Context Clue Signals</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Context Clue Signals</text><text x="4.7" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Definition Clue</text><text x="365.3" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">',' or 'means' gives exact definition</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="11.5" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Example Clue</text><text x="358.5" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">'such as', 'including', 'for instance'</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Contrast Clue</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">'although', 'unlike', 'whereas'</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Result Clue</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Verb effect clarifies word</text></svg>

cheat_sheet.title: Pre vs Re
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Pretest' happens BEFORE lessons; 'Retake' happens AGAIN

cheat_sheet.title: Careless vs Careful
cheat_sheet.formula: -less flips '-ful' completely (hopeful vs hopeless)

cheat_sheet.title: Comma Appositive
cheat_sheet.formula: Words inside commas right after a hard noun often define it

cheat_sheet.title: Mis- Meaning
cheat_sheet.formula: misspell = spell wrongly; misunderstand = get wrong

traps: Never read 'unlike' as meaning similar—an 'unlike X, she was generous' clue gives the OPPOSITE word!
Wait to verify whether '-er' means 'more' (taller) vs. 'one who does' (painter).

examples.title: Morphology Three-Part Breakdown
examples.question: Walkthrough: Examine the diagram splitting RE- + USE + -ABLE. Which phrase matches 'reusable' water bottles?
options: Too heavy for anyone to lift
Built to melt after one sip
Able to be filled and used again safely
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Join 're-' (again) + 'use' + '-able' (can be).

Step 1: re- (again) + use + -able (capable) = able to be used again.

✅ Quick Check: able to be used again.

examples.title: Contrast Clue Word Meaning
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Unlike her timid brother who hid behind the curtains, Layla walked onto the stage and spoke BOLDLY to the crowd.
What does 'timid' most likely mean using the contrast clue?
options: Athletic and fast on the track
Shy and easily nervous around others
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Contrast signal 'unlike' sets timid opposite to 'spoke boldly on stage'.

Step 1: Layla is bold -> timid brother hiding behind curtains = shy/nervous.

✅ Quick Check: Shy and nervous.

examples.title: Mis- Prefix Decoding
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Because the student misread the fraction $3/5$ as $5/3$, his calculation missed the correct answer.
What does 'misread' mean in this math class sentence?
options: Read loudly to the whole class
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Prefix 'mis-' attaches 'wrongly/badly' to the root verb 'read'.

Step 1: mis- (wrongly) + read = read wrongly.

✅ Quick Check: Read wrongly.

examples.title: Appositive Comma Clue
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
During dry summer months, desert foxes forage at twilight, or just after sunset, when sand cools down.
Which definition comes right from the sentence's comma appositive?
options: Just after sunset before full darkness
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Look immediately after ', or ... ,' right beside 'twilight'.

Step 1: Sentence writes: 'at twilight, or just after sunset,'.

✅ Quick Check: just after sunset.

ar.title: تحليل الزوائد (البوادئ واللواحق) وتخمين المعنى من السياق
ar.summary: فهم معاني الكلمات عبر تحليل البوادئ (un-, re-, pre-, dis-, mis-) واللواحق (-ful, -less, -er, -ly)، واستخراج تعريف الكلمة من القرائن السياقية.
goals: تفكيك الكلمات المشتقة إلى سابقة وجذر ولاحقة لمعرفة معناها.
التمييز بين -ful (مملوء بـ) و-less (بلا)، وبين re- (إعادة) وpre- (قبل).
استخدام إشارات التعريف والأمثلة والتضاد داخل الجملة لتفسير الكلمة الصعبة.

concepts.title: جدول معاني البوادئ
concepts.body: تُضاف البادئة في أول الكلمة لتعديل معناها: re- للتكرار، pre- للقبلية، un-/dis- للنفي، mis- للخطأ.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 155" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Prefix + Root + Suffix" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Prefix + Root + Suffix</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="139" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Prefix + Root + Suffix</text><rect x="24" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="70" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#dc2626">Prefix</text><text x="70" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">re-</text><rect x="134" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="180" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Root</text><text x="180" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">use</text><rect x="244" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="290" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#16a34a">Suffix</text><text x="290" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">-able</text><text x="180" y="129" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Meaning: can use again</text></svg>

concepts.title: اللاحقة تحدد نوع الكلمة
concepts.body: تغير اللاحقة نوع الكلمة أو معناها: -less للنفي التام (بلا)، -ly للظرف، -able للقدرة والإمكان.

concepts.title: أربع قرائن سياقية للمفردات
concepts.body: يوفر النص أربع قرائن لتخمين المفردات: التعريف بين فاصلتين، الأمثلة بعد such as، التضاد بعد unlike، والسياق العام.

cheat_sheet.title: الفرق بين pre وre
cheat_sheet.formula: pre- تعني قبل البدء وre- تعني تكرار الفعل

cheat_sheet.title: تعارض اللواحق
cheat_sheet.formula: الكلمة المنتهية بـ -less تعني انعدام الصفة تماماً

cheat_sheet.title: التعريف بالبدل
cheat_sheet.formula: العبارة المحصورة بين فاصلتين بعد كلمة غريبة غالباً تشرحها

cheat_sheet.title: السابقة mis-
cheat_sheet.formula: تدل دائماً على وقوع الفعل على نحو خاطئ

traps: تدل كلمة unlike على العكس التام؛ لا تأخذ الكلمة المقابلة على أنها مرادفة!
تأكد هل اللاحقة -er للفاعل مثل teacher أم للمقارنة مثل faster.

examples.title: تحليل كلمة من سابقة وجذر ولاحقة
examples.question: تطبيق محلول: انظر لمخطط تفكيك كلمة reusable: أي عبارة تفسّر وصف الزجاجة بأنها reusable؟
options: يمكن تعبئتها واستخدامها مرة أخرى بأمان
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: ندمج re- (مرة أخرى) + use (يستخدم) + -able (قابل لـ) = قابل لإعادة الاستخدام.

الخطوة 1: معنى الأجزاء الثلاثة مجتمعة: يمكن استخدامه من جديد.

✅ التحقق من الحل: قابل لإعادة الاستخدام.

examples.title: تخمين الكلمة من قرينة التضاد
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Unlike her timid brother who hid behind the curtains, Layla walked onto the stage and spoke BOLDLY to the crowd.
ما معنى كلمة timid استناداً إلى قرينة التضاد unlike في الجملة؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: أداة التضاد unlike تجعل timid عكس 'تحدثت بجرأة على المسرح'.

الخطوة 1: تختبئ وراء الستارة عكس الجرأة، إذن timid تعني خجول.

✅ التحقق من الحل: خجول.

examples.title: معنى البادئة mis- في الجملة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Because the student misread the fraction $3/5$ as $5/3$, his calculation missed the correct answer.
ما معنى الفعل misread في هذه الجملة؟
options: قرأ بشكل خاطئ أو غير دقيق
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: البادئة mis- تعني فعل الشيء خطأً؛ إذن misread تعني قرأ قراءة خاطئة.

الخطوة 1: قلب الكسر يدل على أنه قرأه بطريقة خاطئة.

✅ التحقق من الحل: قرأ بشكل خاطئ.

examples.title: تعريف الكلمة بين فاصلتين
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
During dry summer months, desert foxes forage at twilight, or just after sunset, when sand cools down.
ما معنى كلمة twilight المستخرج مباشرة من العبارة بين الفاصلتين؟
options: وقت الغسق بعد غروب الشمس بقليل
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: العبارة ', or just after sunset,' تعرف الكلمة السابقة لها مباشرة.

الخطوة 1: التعريف الصريح في النص هو: بعد الغروب بقليل.

✅ التحقق من الحل: بعد الغروب بقليل.

en.title: Collocations, Multi-Meaning Words, Idioms & Phrasal Verbs
en.summary: Pair natural English collocations (make a mistake vs. do homework, pay attention), distinguish homographs in context (bank/park/bat), and decode common Grade 6 idioms and phrasal verbs (give up, look after, piece of cake).
goals: Pair fixed collocations naturally: make a decision / do research / catch a cold / keep a promise.
Determine which dictionary sense of a multi-meaning word fits the sentence.
Interpret figurative phrasal verbs ('put off' = delay, 'look after' = care for) non-literally.

concepts.title: Make vs. Do Collocations
concepts.body: In natural English, DO applies to chores, tasks, and work (do homework, do chores, do research); MAKE applies to creating, deciding, or errors (make a cake, make a choice, make a mistake).
concepts.formula: DO: homework, best, research | MAKE: mistake, plan, choice

concepts.title: Multiple-Meaning Words (Homographs)
concepts.body: Words like 'bark', 'bank', 'spring', and 'bat' hold completely different meanings depending on surrounding clues ('river bank' vs. 'money bank'; 'tree bark' vs. 'dog bark').
concepts.formula: Check neighboring nouns & verbs before translating

concepts.title: Phrasal Verbs & School Idioms
concepts.body: Adding a tiny particle changes a verb's meaning: look FOR (search), look AFTER (take care of), give UP (quit trying), turn DOWN (lower volume or decline).
concepts.formula: look for (search) | look after (care) | give up (quit)

cheat_sheet.title: Decision Verb
cheat_sheet.formula: Always MAKE a decision, never 'do a decision'

cheat_sheet.title: Non-Literal Idiom
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Piece of cake' means EASY, not dessert

cheat_sheet.title: Particle Flip
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Look up' a word means check dictionary, not stare at ceiling

cheat_sheet.title: Sense Test
cheat_sheet.formula: Plug the dictionary meaning back into the sentence

traps: Do NOT translate English phrasal verbs literally ('give up' does not mean handing a gift upward!).
Remember 'do your best' uses DO, while 'make an effort' uses MAKE.

examples.title: Make vs. Do Selection
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Even if we ____ a minor mistake on the first draft, our teacher lets us polish the paragraph neatly.
Which verb completes the fixed collocation '____ a mistake'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Fixed English collocation pairs 'mistake' exclusively with 'make'.

Step 1: Rule: make a mistake (not do a mistake).

✅ Quick Check: make.

examples.title: Multi-Meaning Word 'Bank'
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Wild reeds and green ferns grew thickly along the muddy river ____ where fishermen tied their boats.
In this sentence, what does 'bank' mean?
options: The sloped ground edge beside a river
A sudden tilt of an airplane
examples.explanation:

ar.title: المتلازمات اللفظية والمشترك اللفظي والأفعال المركبة البسيطة
ar.summary: إتقان المتلازمات اللفظية (make/do)، تمييز الكلمات متعددة المعاني من سياقها، وفهم التعابير والأفعال المركبة الشائعة للصف السادس.
goals: اختيار الفعل المصاحب الدقيق للاسم (make/do/take/catch).
تحديد المعنى المقصود للكلمة ذات المعاني المتعددة من خلال القرائن المحيطة.
تفسير الأفعال المركبة والتعابير المجازية بعيداً عن الترجمة الحرفية.

concepts.title: متلازمات الأفعال Make وDo
concepts.body: يُستخدم الفعل do مع المهام والواجبات والبحث، بينما يُستخدم make مع الإنشاء واتخاذ القرار والأخطاء.
concepts.formula:
أزواج شائعة:
$\text{do homework} \mid \text{make a decision}$

concepts.title: الكلمات متعددة المعاني
concepts.body: تختلف دلالة الكلمة الواحدة تماماً حسب الجملة: كلمة bank تعني ضفة نهر أو مصرفاً، وspring تعني ربيعاً أو نبع ماء أو زنبركاً.
concepts.formula:

$\text{انظر للكلمات المجاورة لتحديد المعنى الصحيح}$

concepts.title: الأفعال المركبة والتعابير الاصطلاحية
concepts.body: يتغير معنى الفعل تماماً عند اقترانه بحرف معين: look after يعتني بـ، look for يبحث عن، give up يستسلم.
concepts.formula:
أفعال مركبة مهمة:
$\text{look after (يرعى)} \mid \text{look for (يبحث)} \mid \text{give up (يستسلم)}$

cheat_sheet.title: فعل القرار
cheat_sheet.formula: نقول make a decision لا do a decision

cheat_sheet.title: التعبير المجازي
cheat_sheet.formula: تعبير piece of cake يعني سهل جداً لا قطعة حلوى

cheat_sheet.title: حرف الفعل المركب
cheat_sheet.formula: look for يبحث بينما look after يعتني بـ

cheat_sheet.title: تجربة المعنى
cheat_sheet.formula: عوّض المعنى المقترح في الجملة للتحقق من سلامته

traps: لا تترجم الأفعال المركبة كلمة بكلمة حرفياً.
انتبه: do your best بينما make an effort.

examples.title: اختيار الفعل المتلازم الدقيق
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Even if we ____ a minor mistake on the first draft, our teacher lets us polish the paragraph neatly.
أي فعل يتلازم لغوياً مع كلمة mistake؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: المتلازمة الصحيحة في الإنجليزية هي make a mistake دائماً.

الخطوة 1: نقول make a mistake ولا نقول do.

✅ التحقق من الحل: make.

examples.question:

Wild reeds and green ferns grew thickly along the muddy river ____ where fishermen tied their boats.

While our parents visit Riyadh for two days, my older aunt will ____ our baby brother and water the garden.

examples.title: معنى التعبير المجازي
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
After practicing multiplication facts all month, Tariq grinned and told his friend, 'Today's timed drill was a PIECE OF CAKE!'
ماذا يقصد طارق بتعبير a piece of cake؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تدريب الشهر والابتسامة يوضحان أن المقصود سهولة الاختبار.

الخطوة 1: المعنى الاصطلاحي لـ piece of cake هو شيء بالغ السهولة.

✅ التحقق من الحل: سهل جداً.

en.title: Past Simple, Future (will/going to), Comparatives & Modal Verbs
en.summary: Conjugate regular/irregular Past Simple alongside Present Continuous, choose 'will' vs. 'going to', form accurate -er/-est and more/most comparatives, and use modals (can/must/should/might).
goals: Track time anchors on a timeline: yesterday/last year -> Past Simple; tomorrow -> Future; right now -> Continuous.
Pick '-er + than' for short 1-syllable adjectives vs. 'more ... than' for long 2+ syllable words.
Follow every modal verb (can, must, should) immediately with a BARE base verb (never 'must to go'!).

concepts.title: Time Anchor Tense Timeline
concepts.body: Past anchors ('yesterday', 'in 2022', 'last week') require Past Simple (visited, wrote, went). Future anchors ('next month', 'soon') take 'will + base' or 'be going to + base'.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360.8 145" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Past Simple Anchor" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Past Simple Anchor</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="129" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Past Simple Anchor</text><line x1="36" y1="88" x2="324" y2="88" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="2.2" /><line x1="180" y1="74" x2="180" y2="102" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2" /><text x="52" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Past</text><text x="180" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#0f766e">Now</text><text x="308" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Future</text><circle cx="324.0" cy="88" r="7" fill="#dc2626" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="324.0" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#dc2626">Yesterday</text></svg>

concepts.title: Comparatives & Superlatives Matrix
concepts.body: Compare TWO nouns with '-er than' (short) or 'more ... than' (long). Pick from THREE+ with 'the -est' or 'the most ...'. Remember irregulars: good -> better -> best.
concepts.formula: 2 items: taller / more careful | 3+: tallest / most careful
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Adjective Degrees" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Adjective Degrees</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Adjective Degrees</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">1 syllable (fast)</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">faster than / the fastest</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="11.5" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">2+ syllables (famous)</text><text x="358.5" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">more famous / the most famous</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Irregular good</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">better than / the best</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Irregular bad</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">worse than / the worst</text></svg>

concepts.title: Modal Rule: Base Verb Follows
concepts.body: After should (advice), must (obligation), or can (ability), NEVER add -s, -ed, -ing, or 'to' to the main verb: say 'Students MUST wear badges'.
concepts.formula: must / should / can + BASE VERB (no -s, no -ed, no 'to')
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Modal Checklist" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Modal Checklist</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Modal Checklist</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">should + V1 (Advice)</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">You should drink water.</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">must + V1 (Rule)</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Passengers must fasten belts.</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">can + V1 (Ability)</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Falcons can dive rapidly.</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Error to Avoid</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Never 'must to wears'!</text></svg>

cheat_sheet.title: Did + Base Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: After 'Did' or 'didn't', verb drops -ed -> 'Did he GO?'

cheat_sheet.title: Double Error Trap
cheat_sheet.formula: Never write 'more taller' or 'most best'!

cheat_sheet.title: Good Irregulars
cheat_sheet.formula: went (go), saw (see), wrote (write), bought (buy)

cheat_sheet.title: Plural Pre-Future
cheat_sheet.formula: Use 'are going to' with we/they; 'is going to' with he/she

traps: Never write 'She didn't went' or 'Did you finished?'—'did' already marks past tense!
Never double-mark comparison: choose EITHER '-er' OR 'more', never 'more faster'.

examples.title: Past Negative Trap Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Yesterday afternoon, our robotics club ____ finish testing the ultrasonic sensor because the bell rang early.
Which past negative phrase fills the blank cleanly?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Note the base verb 'finish' right after the blank + past cue 'Yesterday'.

Step 1: 'Yesterday' signals Past -> 'did not' pairs with bare base 'finish'.

✅ Quick Check: did not.

examples.title: Superlative Three-Mountain Check
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Comparing Jabal Sawda, Jabal Al-Lawz, and Jabal Tuwaiq, Jabal Sawda stands as the ____ peak in Saudi Arabia.
Choose the correct superlative form after 'the ____'.
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Three peaks + 'the' calls for superlative '-est' without 'most'.

Step 1: 1-syllable 'high' -> superlative 'the highest' (avoid double 'most highest').

✅ Quick Check: highest.

examples.title: Modal Bare Infinitive Rule
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Before crossing the science lab doorway, every visitor must ____ safety goggles firmly.
Pick the grammatically accurate verb after 'must'.
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Modals (must/should/can) always take an unadorned base verb.

Step 1: Drop 'to', '-ing', and '-s' -> bare 'wear'.

✅ Quick Check: wear.

examples.title: Irregular Verb Past Sentence
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Two weeks ago, my sixth-grade class ____ an interactive exhibit at the King Abdulaziz Center.
Select the irregular past tense verb for 'visit / see'.
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Match time cue 'Two weeks ago' to the true irregular past tense of 'see'.

Step 1: 'See' becomes irregular 'saw' (never 'seed').

✅ Quick Check: saw.

ar.title: الماضي البسيط والمستقبل والمقارنة والأفعال الناقصة
ar.summary: استخدام الماضي البسيط والأفعال الشاذة والمستقبل والمقارنة والتفضيل (-er/-est وmore/most) والأفعال الناقصة (must/should/can).
goals: مطابقة العلامات الزمنية مع الزمن الصحيح (أمس للماضي، غداً للمستقبل، الآن للمستمر).
استخدام -er مع الصفات القصيرة وmore مع الطويلة في المقارنة.
إتباع الأفعال الناقصة بالفعل المجرد دائماً دون to أو s أو ed.

concepts.title: ربط الأزمنة بالعلامات الزمنية
concepts.body: العلامات الماضية كـ yesterday تأخذ الماضي البسيط، بينما علامات المستقبل كـ tomorrow تأخذ will أو going to + المصدر.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360.8 145" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Past Simple Anchor" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Past Simple Anchor</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="129" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Past Simple Anchor</text><line x1="36" y1="88" x2="324" y2="88" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="2.2" /><line x1="180" y1="74" x2="180" y2="102" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2" /><text x="52" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Past</text><text x="180" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#0f766e">Now</text><text x="308" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Future</text><circle cx="324.0" cy="88" r="7" fill="#dc2626" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="324.0" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#dc2626">Yesterday</text></svg>

concepts.title: درجات المقارنة والتفضيل
concepts.body: لمقارنة اثنين: الصفة القصيرة + er + than، والطويلة: more + الصفة + than؛ وللتفضيل: the ...-est أو the most. واحذر الشاذ مثل good/better/best.

concepts.title: قاعدة الأفعال الناقصة
concepts.body: تعبّر الأفعال الناقصة عن النصيحة should والإلزام must والاستطاعة can، ويتبعها دائماً فعل في المصدر المجرد بلا إضافات.

cheat_sheet.title: قاعدة Did
cheat_sheet.formula: بعد did أو didn't يرجع الفعل للمصدر المجرد (didn't go لا didn't went)

cheat_sheet.title: الخطأ المزدوج
cheat_sheet.formula: لا تجمع أبداً بين more و-er في صفة واحدة مثل more taller

cheat_sheet.title: الأفعال الشاذة
cheat_sheet.formula: احفظ تصريفات الماضي الشاذ مثل wrote وwent وsaw

cheat_sheet.title: توافق المستقبل
cheat_sheet.formula: يأتي بعد going to فعل مجرد أيضاً

traps: عند وجود didn't أو did يعود الفعل للأصل المجرد فوراً.
اختر either more OR -er ولا تجمعهما معاً في صفة واحدة.

examples.title: قاعدة النفي في الماضي البسيط
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Yesterday afternoon, our robotics club ____ finish testing the ultrasonic sensor because the bell rang early.
أي صيغة نفي تناسب الجملة الماضية؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: علامة الماضي Yesterday تتطلب did not متبوعة بالمصدر finish الموجود أصلاً.

الخطوة 1: did not تحتاج مصدراً مجرداً بعدها وهو finish.

✅ التحقق من الحل: did not.

examples.title: تفضيل الصفة بين ثلاثة أشياء
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Comparing Jabal Sawda, Jabal Al-Lawz, and Jabal Tuwaiq, Jabal Sawda stands as the ____ peak in Saudi Arabia.
اختر صيغة التفضيل الصحيحة بعد أداة التعريف the:
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: المقارنة بين ثلاث قمم ووجود the يوجبان صيغة التفضيل -est دون إضافة most.

الخطوة 1: الصفة القصيرة high تأخذ est لتصبح highest.

✅ التحقق من الحل: highest.

examples.title: الفعل المجرد بعد الأفعال الناقصة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Before crossing the science lab doorway, every visitor must ____ safety goggles firmly.
اختر الصيغة النحوية السليمة بعد الفعل الناقص must:
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: يتبع الفعل الناقص must الفعل المجرد تماماً دون s أو ing أو to.

الخطوة 1: الصيغة الصحيحة بعد must هي wear فقط.

✅ التحقق من الحل: wear.

examples.title: التصريف الماضي الشاذ
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Two weeks ago, my sixth-grade class ____ an interactive exhibit at the King Abdulaziz Center.
اختر الفعل الصحيح لزمن الماضي منذ أسبوعين:
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عبارة Two weeks ago تدل على الماضي البسيط، وماضي الفعل see الشاذ هو saw.

الخطوة 1: الماضي الصحيح لـ see هو saw لا غير.

✅ التحقق من الحل: saw.

en.title: Passage Synthesis, Multi-Step Inference & Paired Data Texts
en.summary: Synthesize dense B1 informational passages (science/environment/culture), draw warranted multi-clue inferences, and reconcile textual rules with embedded numerical tables.
goals: Eliminate out-of-scope, reversed-cause, and overly broad choices in academic reading.
Verify multi-variable constraints when reading paired notes alongside tables.
Track discourse pronouns and subtle noun referents across complex clauses.

concepts.title: Paired Text + Table Constraint Solver
concepts.body: In B1 paired items, one condition often lives inside the prose note ('students must pay under 3 SAR') while numbers live inside the SVG schedule. Test every row against ALL text rules!
concepts.formula: Note Constraints + Table Values = Single Valid Option

concepts.title: Three-Tier Elimination Strategy
concepts.body: Wrong B1 options usually fall into 3 traps: (1) Extreme words ('always/impossible'), (2) Reversed cause/effect, or (3) True general knowledge NOT supported in the passage.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-61.8 0 483.1 175" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Check Line Proof" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:430px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Check Line Proof</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="159" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Check Line Proof</text><rect x="55" y="42" width="260" height="36" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.8" /><text x="185" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">Option Filter</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="68" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="18" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="26.3" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Trap 1: Extreme 'always'</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="184" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="134" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="188.6" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Trap 2: Reverses cause</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="300" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="250" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="340.1" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Trap 3: Unstated claim</text></svg>

concepts.title: Complex Discourse Referents
concepts.body: When multiple nouns appear ('mentors praised the code for its error handling'), verify both grammar number (singular 'its') and semantic fit (does a mentor have error handling, or does code?).

cheat_sheet.title: Hidden Prose Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: Read the short note ABOVE the table just as carefully as the rows

cheat_sheet.title: Eliminate Extremes
cheat_sheet.formula: Suspicious options with 'completely / never / everyone' usually fail

cheat_sheet.title: Active vs Passive Link
cheat_sheet.formula: Ask WHO performs the verb when resolving 'they/them'

cheat_sheet.title: Direct Evidence
cheat_sheet.formula: Re-check the clause mentioning 'compared with' or 'whereas'

traps: Even if a fact is scientifically true in daily life, reject it on Reading Comprehension unless the passage itself supports it.
Don't misread 'less than 10 minutes' as accepting 10+ minutes.

examples.title: Paired Note & Grid Audit
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
A 14-year-old student with 3 SAR in pocket must join a STEM workshop starting BEFORE 10:00 AM.
Examining the Workshop Grid card, which hall meets ALL three constraints?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Verify Age 14 fit + Fare <= 3 SAR + Start < 10:00 AM simultaneously.

Step 1: Hall A needs Age 15+; Hall B costs 4 SAR; Hall C starts 11:00 AM; Hall D fits all 3 (Age 12+, 2 SAR, 9 AM).

✅ Quick Check: Hall D.
