examples.title: Cause-Effect Inference
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Noticeably fewer coastal seabirds nested on the island last spring; simultaneously, stray cats spotted near the cliff burrows tripled after a ferry dock opened nearby.
Which inference best explains the drop in seabird nesting?
options: Seabirds suddenly forgot how to fly over seawater
Opening a ferry dock improved fish habitats for cats
Cliff stones dissolved completely within twelve months
Increased predation pressure from newly arriving stray cats disturbed nesting sites
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Connect simultaneous events causally without inventing biological impossibilities.

Step 1: Ferry dock -> stray cats multiplied near burrows -> predation drove birds off cliffs.

✅ Quick Check: Cat predation disturbed nesting.

examples.title: Eliminating Extreme Distractors
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Reverse-osmosis desalination plants using solar arrays cut fossil energy demand by 38% over five years, yet coastal cities still rely on grid backups during dusty cloudy weeks.
Which statement accurately reflects the passage without overstating?
options: Fossil electricity vanished from every Saudi coastline five years ago
Desalination plants stopped supplying drinking water in winter
Solar desalination significantly cuts fuel use but still needs backup power in overcast weather
Solar arrays run at 100% power throughout thick dust storms
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Respect both clauses: 38% reduction + 'yet' qualifier noting cloudy-week grid backups.

Step 1: Avoids extreme absolutes ('vanished', '100%') and balances reduction with backup need.

✅ Quick Check: Balanced qualified statement.

examples.title: الدمج بين النص والجدول
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
A 14-year-old student with 3 SAR in pocket must join a STEM workshop starting BEFORE 10:00 AM.
من جدول الورش المرفق، أي قاعة تحقق الشروط الثلاثة معاً (العمر 14، التكلفة بحد أقصى 3 ريالات، وقبل الساعة العاشرة)؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نختبر كل قاعة ضد الشروط الثلاثة معاً: السن والوقت والميزانية.

الخطوة 1: القاعة D الوحيدة المناسبة: تبدأ 9 صباحاً، تكلفتها ريالان، وتقبل من عمر 12.

✅ التحقق من الحل: القاعة D.

examples.title: الاستنتاج السببي الدقيق
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Noticeably fewer coastal seabirds nested on the island last spring; simultaneously, stray cats spotted near the cliff burrows tripled after a ferry dock opened nearby.
ما الاستنتاج الأدق الذي يفسّر تراجع تعشيش الطيور البحرية؟
options: نسيت الطيور فجأة كيف تطير فوق البحر
تآكلت صخور المنحدر وذابت خلال عام
ازدياد ضغط الافتراس من القطط الضالة بعد فتح مرسى العبارات أزعج الأعشاش
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تربط القرينة الزمنية فتح المرسى بزيادة القطط المفترسة قرب جحور الأعشاش مما طرد الطيور.

الخطوة 1: افتراس القطط المتزايد يفسّر انخفاض التعشيش منطقياً.

✅ التحقق من الحل: ازدياد الافتراس من القطط.

examples.title: فك التباس الضمير الجمع
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Before uploading vintage maps to the digital archive, librarians dusted brittle frames carefully so scanners could photograph them clearly without glare.
إلى ماذا يشير الضمير them في الجملة؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نحدد المفعول به الذي تصوّره الماسحات الضوئية لحفظه في الأرشيف الرقمي.

الخطوة 1: الخرائط القديمة هي التي تُمسح ضوئياً لا الأمناء ولا الماسحات.

✅ التحقق من الحل: الخرائط القديمة.

examples.title: استبعاد التعميم الخاطئ
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Reverse-osmosis desalination plants using solar arrays cut fossil energy demand by 38% over five years, yet coastal cities still rely on grid backups during dusty cloudy weeks.
أي عبارة تعكس مضمون النص بدقة ودون مبالغة؟
options: اختفت الكهرباء التقليدية تماماً من كل السواحل قبل خمس سنوات
توقفت المحطات عن تزويد المدن بالماء شتاءً
تخفض التحلية الشمسية الوقود بدرجة كبيرة لكنها لا تزال تحتاج احتياطياً أثناء الغبار والغيوم
تعمل الألواح بكفاءة 100% وسط العواصف الترابية
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تجمع الإجابة السليمة بين توفير الطاقة بنسبة 38% واستثناء الجملة الثانية حول الحاجة للاحتياط أثناء الغيوم.

الخطوة 1: الجمع بين الإنجاز والقيد يحفظ أمانة النص.

✅ التحقق من الحل: تخفض الوقود مع الحاجة للاحتياط.

en.title: Central Thesis, Rhetorical Purpose, Author Tone & Paragraph Cohesion
en.summary: Extract multi-paragraph central claims, diagnose why an author includes an anecdote or statistic, recognize nuanced B1 tone (skeptical/cautious/optimistic/urgent), and order coherent paragraphs smoothly.
goals: Ask 'WHAT WORK does this statistic/anecdote perform in paragraph 2?' rather than repeating its literal content.
Read evaluative verbs and modal hedges ('appears promising, though hurdles remain') to identify balanced/cautious tone.
Sequence shuffled sentences using reference chains ('This problem' follows the problem definition!).

concepts.title: Why Authors Cite Evidence
concepts.body: Authors insert opening stories to hook readers, statistics to ground abstract claims in numbers, and counter-arguments to appear fair before refuting objections.

concepts.title: Nuanced B1 Writer Tone
concepts.body: Contrast extreme anger/enthusiasm with measured academic tones: Cautiously Optimistic ('promising yet requires study'), Critical ('flawed oversight'), Analytical ('driven by three factors').
concepts.formula: Words Reveal Attitude: Flawed = Critical | Promising yet = Cautious

concepts.title: Paragraph Cohesion Chains
concepts.body: Anchor Topic Sentence #1 broadly, track pronoun chains ('This approach...' / 'As a result...'), and finish with Concluding Synthesis.
concepts.formula: Broad Claim $\to$ Named Method $\to$ 'This method...' $\to$ Outcome

cheat_sheet.title: Evidence Function
cheat_sheet.formula: Ask 'WHY did writer put this number here?'

cheat_sheet.title: Cautious Optimism
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Promising gains, though gaps remain' = cautiously optimistic

cheat_sheet.title: Cohesion Link
cheat_sheet.formula: 'This barrier' can NEVER be sentence #1 of a paragraph

cheat_sheet.title: Thesis vs Topic
cheat_sheet.formula: Thesis states the writer's specific CLAIM about the topic

traps: Never choose 'to criticize X harshly' when the author merely points out mild practical limitations politely.
A topic like 'Desalination' is NOT a thesis; a thesis takes a stance ('Hybrid solar desalination lowers grid stress efficiently').

examples.title: Author Purpose of an Example
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
To show that rainwater gardens work outside lush forests, the article highlights Taif's terrace ponds capturing summer flash floods and watering local apricot orchards.
Why does the author mention Taif's terrace ponds?
options: To complain that Taif lacks summer sunshine
To prove apricots grow exclusively underwater
To demonstrate concretely that water-catching landscapes succeed even in dry highland regions
To discourage residents from planting orchards
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Read the clause right before the example: 'To show that rainwater gardens work outside lush forests...'.

Step 1: Direct explicit bridge states example proves effectiveness outside wet forests.

✅ Quick Check: Proves success in dry highlands.
examples.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Bridge Cue Analysis" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Bridge Cue Analysis</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Bridge Cue Analysis</text><text x="8.1" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Stated Reason</text><text x="361.9" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">show gardens work outside lush forests</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Concrete Case</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Taif terrace ponds</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Measured Payoff</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">waters apricot orchards</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Author Move</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Prove feasibility via example</text></svg>

examples.title: Identifying Measured Tone
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Pilot battery ferries reduced harbor emissions remarkably, though engineers caution that high summer salt humidity still demands sturdier casing designs.
Which phrase best describes the writer's tone?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Blend positive validation ('remarkably reduced') with realistic engineering constraint ('though... demands sturdier').

Step 1: Balanced praise + realistic caveat = cautious/measured optimism.

✅ Quick Check: Measured / cautiously optimistic.
examples.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-97.6 0 522.3 175" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Cautiously Optimistic" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:430px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Cautiously Optimistic</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="159" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Cautiously Optimistic</text><rect x="55" y="42" width="260" height="36" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.8" /><text x="185" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">Tone Clues</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="68" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="18" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="-2.7" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Praise: reduced remarkably</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="184" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="134" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="197.2" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Hedge: though engineers caution</text><line x1="185" y1="78" x2="300" y2="108" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.5" /><rect x="250" y="108" width="102" height="44" rx="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="1.5" /><text x="360.5" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">No insult / anger</text></svg>

examples.title: Paragraph Flow & Coherence
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
(1) However, these open canals lost water rapidly under noon heat. (2) Ancient oasis farmers originally carried spring water through uncovered clay ditches. (3) Covering canals underground eventually cut evaporation almost in half.
Which order creates a smooth, coherent paragraph?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Sentence 2 introduces 'uncovered clay ditches' -> Sentence 1 calls them 'these open canals' -> Sentence 3 gives final solution.

Step 1: Only (2) has no dangling reference word; (1) must follow (2) to resolve 'these open canals'.

✅ Quick Check: (2) -> (1) -> (3).

examples.title: Supporting Claim Evidence
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Claim: Dedicated bus lanes persuade private drivers to switch to public transit cleanly during morning rush hours.
Which finding would BEST strengthen the writer's claim?
options: Rain fell on Tuesdays during winter
After dedicating a bus lane, morning bus speeds doubled and daily car commuting dropped 28%
Drivers bought shiny coffee cups at gas stations
Buses carry bright green roofs painted in factories
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Strong evidence directly measures BOTH fast buses AND drivers switching from cars.

Step 1: Data directly confirms modal shift (-28% cars) after bus lanes opened.

✅ Quick Check: 28% drop in car commuting.
examples.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Evidence Strength" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Evidence Strength</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Evidence Strength</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Writer Claim</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Bus lanes shift car drivers</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Required Data</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Driver behavior change %</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Best Proof</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">-28% car commutes + 2x bus speed</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Irrelevant</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Paint colors / weather</text></svg>

ar.title: الأطروحة الرئيسة والهدف البلاغي ونبرة الكاتب وتماسك الفقرة
ar.summary: استخلاص الأطروحة الرئيسة، تحليل سبب إدراج الكاتب لقصة أو إحصائية، تمييز النبرة الدقيقة (متشكك/متفائل/تحذيري)، وترتيب جمل الفقرة المتماسكة.
goals: السؤال: لماذا أضاف الكاتب هذه القصة أو الرقم؟ لدعم حجة أم لعرض مقارنة؟
قراءة الأفعال والنعوت الحذرة لتحديد النبرة (متفائل بحذر، موضوعي، ناقد).
ربط أسماء الإشارة في ترتيب الجمل بحيث يسبق الموصوفُ الإشارةَ إليه.

concepts.title: وظيفة الشواهد والأمثلة في الفقرة
concepts.body: يُدرج الكاتب القصة الافتتاحية لجذب الانتباه، والأرقام لدعم الدعوى موضوعياً، والرأي المعارض لمناقشته والرد عليه.

examples.title: تحليل وظيفة المثال في المقال
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
To show that rainwater gardens work outside lush forests, the article highlights Taif's terrace ponds capturing summer flash floods and watering local apricot orchards.
لماذا أورد الكاتب مثال برك المصاطب في الطائف؟
options: لإثبات عملي لنجاح حدائق تجميع الأمطار حتى في المرتفعات شبه الجافة
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الجملة السابقة للمثال تصرح بوظيفته: لإثبات نجاح هذه التقنية خارج الغابات الممطرة.

الخطوة 1: وظيفة المثال توضيحية لإثبات إمكانية التطبيق في المناطق الجافة.

✅ التحقق من الحل: إثبات نجاحها في المناطق الجافة.

examples.title: تمييز النبرة المتزنة الحذرة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Pilot battery ferries reduced harbor emissions remarkably, though engineers caution that high summer salt humidity still demands sturdier casing designs.
ما الوصف الأدق لنبرة الكاتب في العبارة؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الجمع بين الإشادة بالإنجاز (خفض الانبعاثات بشكل ملحوظ) والتنبيه الواقعي للعائق الهندسي يعكس نبرة متفائلة بحذر.

الخطوة 1: الموضوعية تظهر في ذكر الإنجاز والتحدي معاً.

✅ التحقق من الحل: متزنة ومتفائلة بحذر.

examples.title: ترتيب جمل الفقرة المترابطة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
(1) However, these open canals lost water rapidly under noon heat. (2) Ancient oasis farmers originally carried spring water through uncovered clay ditches. (3) Covering canals underground eventually cut evaporation almost in half.
أي ترتيب يحقق التسلسل المنطقي والتماسك المرجعي للفقرة؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الجملة (2) تقدم الخنادق المكشوفة أولاً، فتعود عليها (1) بـ 'هذه القنوات'، ثم تأتي (3) بالحل النهائي.

الخطوة 1: المرجع يفرض تقدم (2) على (1)، ثم النتيجة في (3).

✅ التحقق من الحل: (2) -> (1) -> (3).

examples.title: اختيار الدليل الداعم للأطروحة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Claim: Dedicated bus lanes persuade private drivers to switch to public transit cleanly during morning rush hours.
أي نتيجة بحثية تمنح أطروحة الكاتب أقوى دعم ممكن؟
options: بعد تخصيص مسار الحافلات تضاعفت سرعتها وانخفض تنقل السيارات الخاصة 28%
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الدليل القوي يقيس النتيجة المقصودة بالأرقام: ارتفاع سرعة الحافلات وانخفاض الاعتماد على السيارات الخاصة.

الخطوة 1: النتيجة العددية المباشرة تدعم الدعوى بقوة.

✅ التحقق من الحل: انخفاض السيارات 28%.

en.title: Persuasive Rhetoric, Counterarguments & Cross-Text Synthesis
en.summary: Analyze how persuasive texts combine logos/data with concessions ('While critics note X, recent results show Y'), and compare agreements or disagreements across short paired viewpoints (Passage A vs. Passage B).
goals: Identify concessions ('Although startup cost is high...') used before rebuttals.
Pinpoint the exact point where Viewpoint A and Viewpoint B agree vs. collide.
Check logical validity—ensure conclusions follow without hasty generalizations.

concepts.title: Concession + Rebuttal Blueprint
concepts.body: Strong persuasive essays look fair by granting a real point to critics ('While solar batteries cost more initially...'), then pivoting ('however, five-year savings outweigh upfront expense').

concepts.title: Comparing Passage A vs. Passage B
concepts.body: Draw a mental Venn check: what does BOTH Speaker A and Speaker B accept as true, versus where do their recommendations sharply diverge?
concepts.formula: Both Accept Fact X | Disagreement Focus = Solution Y vs Z

cheat_sheet.title: Pivot Signal
cheat_sheet.formula: Main author stance ALWAYS follows 'however / yet' after a concession

cheat_sheet.title: Dual Passages
cheat_sheet.formula: Look for shared goal even when methods clash

cheat_sheet.title: Sample Audit
cheat_sheet.formula: Question tiny sample sizes or single-person quotes

cheat_sheet.title: Objective Evaluation
cheat_sheet.formula: Strong arguments pair concrete mechanisms with realistic trade-offs

traps: Never mistake the concession sentence ('Critics worry tablets distract eyes...') for the author's own conclusion!
Notice when Speaker B responds directly to Speaker A—mark whether B rejects A's premise or merely prioritizes a different constraint.

examples.title: Spotting the Author's Concession
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
While some coaches worry afternoon robotics clubs cut into sports practice, school records show robotics members maintain higher gym attendance than average.
How does the sentence structure respond to coaches' worry?
options: It blames gym teachers for low exam grades
It acknowledges their concern first, then refutes it using attendance records
It changes the subject to kitchen menus
It agrees completely and cancels all robotics clubs
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Identify 'While' conceding the concern, followed by contradicting school record data.

Step 1: 'While some coaches worry...' = concession; 'school records show higher attendance' = data rebuttal.

✅ Quick Check: Acknowledges then refutes.

examples.title: Dual Passage Common Ground
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Text A: Municipal parks must plant drought-hardy acacia trees instead of lawns to conserve groundwater. Text B: While grassy picnic fields attract families, cities should expand drought-tolerant acacia groves around neighborhood edges.
What single point do Text A and Text B CLEARLY share?
options: Every grass picnic field must be paved with concrete
Acacia groves waste excessive groundwater daily
Families dislike resting inside shaded city parks
Cities should plant drought-tolerant acacia trees to save water
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Isolate overlapping recommendations present in BOTH Text A and Text B.

Step 1: Text A backs acacia; Text B also backs expanding acacia groves.

✅ Quick Check: Both endorse acacia.

examples.title: Flawed Evidence Critique
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Because the four students standing near the chess table preferred math over history, the reporter concluded that every ninth-grade pupil dislikes history.
Why is the reporter's conclusion logically weak?
options: Chess tables require accurate clocks to operate cleanly
Reporters are forbidden from talking near libraries
It draws an extreme generalization about all students from four chess players
History books contain fewer chapters than geometry texts
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Spot the leap from tiny biased group (4 chess players) to absolute claim ('every ninth-grade pupil').

Step 1: Sample size = 4 + biased setting -> hasty generalization.

✅ Quick Check: Hasty generalization.

examples.title: Rhetorical Question Effect
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
In a speech advocating bike lanes, a student asks: 'Would any parent want their child dodging fast trucks just to reach school safely?'
Why does the speaker open with a question expecting an obvious 'No'?
options: Because she genuinely forgets whether trucks drive fast
To collect numerical street-width counts orally
To engage listeners emotionally and unite them behind safer bike lanes
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Rhetorical questions align audience values quickly without seeking literal replies.

Step 1: No parent wants hazard -> instantly unites listeners behind bike-lane safety.

✅ Quick Check: Builds emotional alignment.

ar.title: بلاغة الإقناع ودحض الحجج المضادة والتركيب بين نصين
ar.summary: تحليل استراتيجيات الإقناع والتسليم الجزئي للحجج المضادة ثم تفنيدها، والمقارنة بين نصين متقابلين لتحديد مواطن الاتفاق والاختلاف.
goals: تحديد مواضع التسليم الجزئي بالرأي المخالف قبل تفنيده بالأدلة.
رصد نقطة الاتفاق ونقطة الاختلاف الدقيقة بين نصي A وB.
كشف التعميمات المتسرعة في الحجج الإقناعية.

examples.title: تمييز التسليم الجزئي والرد
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
While some coaches worry afternoon robotics clubs cut into sports practice, school records show robotics members maintain higher gym attendance than average.
كيف تتعامل الجملة مع قلق المدربين؟
options: تعترف بقلقهم مبدئياً ثم تدحضه بسجلات الحضور الفعلية
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تبدأ الجملة بالتسليم بقلقهم عبر While ثم تفنّده بسجلات الحضور الأعلى.

الخطوة 1: التركيب يجمع الاعتراف المبدئي بالرد المدعوم بالبيانات.

✅ التحقق من الحل: اعتراف ثم تفنيد.

examples.title: تحديد نقطة الاتفاق بين نصين
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Text A: Municipal parks must plant drought-hardy acacia trees instead of lawns to conserve groundwater. Text B: While grassy picnic fields attract families, cities should expand drought-tolerant acacia groves around neighborhood edges.
ما النقطة الواضحة التي يتفق عليها النصان A وB معاً؟
options: يجب رصف كل المسطحات الخضراء بالإسمنت
تستهلك أشجار الأكاسيا مياهاً جوفية غزيرة
تكره العائلات الجلوس في الحدائق المظللة
ينبغي للمدن زراعة أشجار الأكاسيا المتحملة للجفاف لتوفير المياه
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: يتفق النصان بوضوح على جدوى التوسع في زراعة أشجار الأكاسيا المقاومة للجفاف، ويختلفان فقط في حذف العشب كلياً أم إبقائه.

الخطوة 1: المساحة المشتركة هي تأييد زراعة الأكاسيا.

✅ التحقق من الحل: تأييد زراعة الأكاسيا.

examples.title: نقد الاستنتاج من عينة صغيرة
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Because the four students standing near the chess table preferred math over history, the reporter concluded that every ninth-grade pupil dislikes history.
لماذا يُعد استنتاج المراسل ضعيفاً منطقياً؟
options: تحتاج طاولات الشطرنج إلى ساعات دقيقة
يُمنع المراسلون من التحدث قرب المكتبة
يبني تعميماً مطلقاً على جميع الطلاب انطلاقاً من أربعة فقط قرب طاولة الشطرنج
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: القفز من رأي أربعة طلاب فقط إلى تعميم يشمل كل طلاب الصف مغالطة التعميم المتسرع.

الخطوة 1: العينة بالغة الصغر وغير ممثلة للجميع.

✅ التحقق من الحل: تعميم متسرع من عينة صغيرة.

examples.title: أثر السؤال البلاغي في الإقناع
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
In a speech advocating bike lanes, a student asks: 'Would any parent want their child dodging fast trucks just to reach school safely?'
لماذا افتتح المتحدث خطابه بسؤال استنكاري إجابته الواضحة لا؟
options: لإشراك المستمعين عاطفياً وحشد تأييدهم لمسارات دراجات آمنة
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: السؤال البلاغي لا ينتظر جواباً بل يحرك ضمير المستمعين ويجمعهم فوراً حول أهمية الأمان المروري.

الخطوة 1: السؤال الاستنكاري يقوي الإقناع بمشاركة الجمهور.

✅ التحقق من الحل: جذب التأييد العاطفي للمطلب.

en.title: Academic Context Vocabulary & Greek/Latin Roots
en.summary: Determine precise B1 academic vocabulary (mitigate, scarce, resilient, crucial, abundant) through contrast/cause context, and decode scientific/literary words via classical roots (bio-, geo-, therm-, struct-, port-, vis-).
goals: Use clause logic and academic tone to choose precise B1 synonyms in context.
Break unfamiliar academic terms into Root + Affix (bio- = life, hydro- = water, port = carry, vis = see).
Avoid false-friend surface guesses when a second clause narrows a technical sense.

concepts.title: Academic Contrast Clues
concepts.body: Contrast conjunctions ('nevertheless', 'whereas', 'despite') signal that an unfamiliar word carries the opposite charge of the known clause.
concepts.formula: Known Concept $\xrightarrow{\text{whereas / despite}}$ Opposite New Word
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Academic Vocabulary Bank" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Academic Vocabulary Bank</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Academic Vocabulary Bank</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">abundant <> scarce</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">plentiful vs rare/short</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="11.5" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">resilient <> fragile</text><text x="358.5" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">recovers fast vs breaks easily</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">crucial <> trivial</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">essential vs unimportant</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">mitigate <> worsen</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">reduce harm vs intensify</text></svg>

concepts.title: Classical Root Families
concepts.body: One root unlocks dozens of exam words: PORT = carry (export, portable), STRUCT = build (construct, infrastructure), VIS/VID = see (visible, evidence), AQUA/HYDRO = water.
concepts.formula: Root = Core Anchor | Affix = Grammar & Direction
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 155" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Root Family Example" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:360px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Root Family Example</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="139" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Root Family Example</text><rect x="24" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="70" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#dc2626">Prefix</text><text x="70" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">trans-</text><rect x="134" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="180" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Root</text><text x="180" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">port</text><rect x="244" y="48" width="92" height="54" rx="8" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.7"/><text x="290" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#16a34a">Suffix</text><text x="290" y="89" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#231942">-ation</text><text x="180" y="129" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Meaning: carry across</text></svg>

concepts.title: Degree & Register Precision
concepts.body: Pay attention to intensity: 'chilly' vs. 'frigid', 'hesitant' vs. 'terrified'. Match the EXACT degree of emotion or urgency shown by supporting clues.
concepts.formula: Check Intensity Scale: Mild | Moderate | Extreme

cheat_sheet.title: Root Anchor
cheat_sheet.formula: bio (life), geo (earth), therm (heat), script (write)

cheat_sheet.title: Despite Signal
cheat_sheet.formula: 'Despite scarce rain, crops grew' -> scarce MUST mean limited

cheat_sheet.title: Positive/Negative Check
cheat_sheet.formula: Eliminate words with wrong positive/negative charge first

cheat_sheet.title: Substitute Test
cheat_sheet.formula: Plug the candidate synonym right into the blank

traps: Do not replace a moderate verb ('reduced') with an extreme exaggeration ('obliterated') unless clues support complete destruction.
Check whether 're-' on a word is an actual prefix ('rebuild') vs. accidental letters ('reach').

examples.title: Academic Word 'Resilient'
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Even after harsh winter sandstorms snapped young twigs, the native ghaf trees proved remarkably RESILIENT, sprouting fresh green shoots within weeks.
In this botanical report, what does 'resilient' mean?
options: Impossible to plant outside wet glasshouses
Fragile and permanently destroyed by light wind
Able to recover rapidly after damage or stress
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Contrast harsh storm snapping twigs with fast green regrowth weeks later.

Step 1: Trees bounced back quickly after damage -> resilient = recovers rapidly.

✅ Quick Check: Able to recover quickly.

examples.title: Latin Root Transportation
examples.question: Walkthrough: Use the morphology card 'trans- + port + -ation'. Using root meanings, what does 'portable' solar gear mean?
options: Light enough to carry from camp to camp easily
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Combine root 'port' (carry) with suffix '-able' (capable of).

Step 1: port (carry) + -able (can be) = able to be carried easily.

✅ Quick Check: easy to carry.

examples.title: Whereas Contrast Inference
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Surface desert sands appear BARREN at noon, whereas cooler night air reveals rich communities of nocturnal beetles and desert hedgehogs.
Using 'whereas' and surrounding contrast clues, what does 'barren' suggest?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Contrast 'barren' at noon with 'rich communities' revealed at night.

Step 1: Opposite of 'rich communities' -> barren = empty/lifeless.

✅ Quick Check: Empty / lifeless.

examples.title: Precision Intensity Choice
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Unlike ordinary rainfall that quickly drains away, yesterday's ____ cloudburst flooded underpasses within twenty minutes.
Which adjective matches the extreme severity clue 'flooded underpasses in twenty minutes'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Match extreme consequence (20-min flash flood) to intense rain adjective.

Step 1: Flooding underpasses demands intense adjective -> torrential.

✅ Quick Check: torrential.

ar.title: مفردات السياق الأكاديمي والجذور اليونانية واللاتينية
ar.summary: تحديد معاني المفردات الأكاديمية الدقيقة من سياق التضاد والسببية، وتفكيك الكلمات العلمية عبر جذورها اللاتينية واليونانية.
goals: توظيف منطق الجملة والتضاد لاختيار المرادف الأكاديمي الدقيق.
تحليل الجذور الشائعة في النصوص العلمية مثل bio وgeo وport وvis.
الاعتماد على القرينة السياقية الكاملة لا التخمين السطحي للشكل.

examples.title: معنى كلمة resilient في السياق
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Even after harsh winter sandstorms snapped young twigs, the native ghaf trees proved remarkably RESILIENT, sprouting fresh green shoots within weeks.
في هذا التقرير النباتي، ما معنى كلمة resilient؟
options: قادر على التعافي السريع بعد الضرر والشدة
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: إنبات براعم خضراء جديدة سريعاً بعد العاصفة القاسية يوضح القدرة العالية على التعافي والصمود.

الخطوة 1: التعافي السريع بعد التلف هو معنى resilient.

✅ التحقق من الحل: قادر على التعافي السريع.

examples.question: تطبيق محلول: استخدم جذر port (ينقل/يحمل) لتحديد معنى صفة portable للألواح الشمسية:
options: خفيفة يسهل حملها ونقلها من موقع لآخر
examples.explanation:

examples.title: الاستدلال عبر أداة التناقض whereas
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Surface desert sands appear BARREN at noon, whereas cooler night air reveals rich communities of nocturnal beetles and desert hedgehogs.
باستخدام أداة المقابلة whereas، ماذا توحي كلمة barren؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: تضع whereas الكلمة مقابل 'مجتمعات حيوية غنية ليلاً'، إذن barren تعني قاحلة وخالية ظاهرياً.

الخطوة 1: الضد السياقي للغنى الحيوي هو القحط والفراغ.

✅ التحقق من الحل: قاحلة وخالية من الحياة.

examples.title: دقة درجة المفردة السياقية
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Unlike ordinary rainfall that quickly drains away, yesterday's ____ cloudburst flooded underpasses within twenty minutes.
أي صفة تلائم شدة المطر الذي أغرق الأنفاق في عشرين دقيقة؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: النتيجة العنيفة (غرق الأنفاق في دقائق) تتطلب صفة بالغة الشدة وهي torrential.

الخطوة 1: الصفات الخفيفة لا تفسّر الفيضان السريع.

✅ التحقق من الحل: torrential.

en.title: Nuanced Synonyms, Idioms, Prepositional Phrases & Register
en.summary: Differentiate B1 synonyms by usage nuance, decode academic and everyday idioms ('on the fence', 'cut corners', 'silver lining'), pair fixed prepositional verbs (rely ON, insist ON, capable OF), and shift informal slang into formal register.
goals: Select prepositions fixed to verbs/adjectives: interested IN, responsible FOR, rely ON, keen ON, suffer FROM.
Decode B1 figurative idioms from discourse clues rather than literal word meaning.
Replace casual chat phrasing ('loads of stuff') with crisp academic register ('extensive data').

concepts.title: Fixed Verb/Adjective Prepositions
concepts.body: Certain verbs and adjectives lock permanently to specific prepositions: depend/rely ON, apologize FOR, consist OF, capable OF, afraid OF, interested IN.
concepts.formula: rely ON | capable OF | responsible FOR | suffer FROM
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Preposition Lock Table" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Preposition Lock Table</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Preposition Lock Table</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">depend / rely / insist</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + ON</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">capable / proud / aware</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + OF</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">responsible / apologize</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + FOR</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">interested / succeed</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + IN</text></svg>

concepts.title: Figurative Idioms in Prose
concepts.body: Common B1 idioms carry clear meanings: 'cut corners' = skip careful steps cheaply, 'on the fence' = undecided, 'silver lining' = good outcome inside setback.
concepts.formula: Idiom = Figurative Concept Clued by Surrounding Tone

concepts.title: Formal vs. Informal Register
concepts.body: Academic reports avoid slang ('kids', 'totally awesome', 'messed up') and pick concise formal phrasing ('students', 'remarkable', 'overlooked').
concepts.formula: Casual ('a bunch of stuff') $\to$ Formal ('numerous samples')

cheat_sheet.title: Consist OF Rule
cheat_sheet.formula: Say 'consists OF 4 layers', never 'consists from'

cheat_sheet.title: Transfer Trap
cheat_sheet.formula: Wait before translating Arabic prepositions directly into English

cheat_sheet.title: Tone Cue for Idiom
cheat_sheet.formula: Is the team celebrating or complaining right before the idiom?

cheat_sheet.title: Formal Essay Choice
cheat_sheet.formula: Reject contractions and slang when rewriting formal lab notes

traps: Arabic 'يعتمد على' nicely matches 'rely ON', whereas 'يهتم بـ' uses 'interested IN'—do NOT use 'with'!
Avoid 'cut corners' as meaning geometry—it specifically means sacrificing quality to take a shortcut.

examples.title: Locked Preposition Choice
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Engine designers proved that the compact hydrogen fuel cell is capable ____ powering a bus across steep mountain roads.
Which preposition locks permanently after 'capable'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Rule: adjective 'capable' is always followed by 'of + noun/-ing'.

Step 1: Pattern: 'is capable OF powering...' (never 'to' or 'with').

✅ Quick Check: of.

examples.title: Idiom 'Cut Corners'
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Our chemistry coach warned that lab teams who CUT CORNERS by skipping goggles and scale calibration produce unreliable results.
What does 'cut corners' mean in this lab warning?
options: Paint lab table corners bright blue
Fold paper squares into sharp triangles
Skip careful safety or quality steps to save time or effort
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Check the explicit appositive example: 'by skipping goggles and scale calibration'.

Step 1: Skipping careful steps to rush = cut corners.

✅ Quick Check: Skip careful steps.

examples.title: Formal Academic Register
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Casual draft: 'The student science team found out tons of cool stuff about desert beetle wings collecting morning fog.'
Which revision converts the underlined casual phrasing into crisp formal report English?
options: gathered substantial evidence regarding desert beetle wing structures
grabbed huge heaps of neat little things about bug backs
copied random stuff off social chats
sniffed around for crazy awesome secrets
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Replace vague casual nouns ('tons of cool stuff') with exact academic terms ('substantial evidence').

Step 1: Eliminate 'tons', 'cool', 'neat', 'crazy', 'stuff' -> formal 'gathered substantial evidence'.

✅ Quick Check: gathered substantial evidence...

examples.title: Slight Verb Nuance
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Before approving the bridge blueprint, civil engineers will ____ every weld joint under laser sensors to ensure zero hidden cracks.
Which precise verb fits detailed technical checking?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: 'Inspect' means examine carefully for defects, whereas 'glance' means look briefly.

Step 1: Detailed safety scan with laser sensors -> inspect.

✅ Quick Check: inspect.

ar.title: الفروق الدلالية الدقيقة والتعابير الاصطلاحية وحروف الجر المتلازمة
ar.summary: التمييز بين الفروق الدقيقة للمترادفات، تفسير التعابير الاصطلاحية، ضبط حروف الجر الملازمة للأفعال والصفات (rely on / capable of)، وتحويل الأسلوب للغة الرسمية.
goals: ضبط حروف الجر الثابتة مع الأفعال والصفات الأكاديمية.
فهم التعابير المجازية البلاغية من سياق الموقف.
الارتقاء بالصياغة من الأسلوب العامي اليومي إلى الأسلوب الأكاديمي الرسمي.

concepts.title: تلازم حروف الجر الأكاديمية
concepts.body: تقترن بعض الأفعال والصفات بحروف جر محددة لا تتغير: rely on يعتمد على، capable of قادر على، consist of يتكون من، interested in مهتم بـ.
concepts.formula:
تلازمات ثابتة:
$\text{rely ON} \mid \text{capable OF} \mid \text{responsible FOR}$
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Preposition Lock Table" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Preposition Lock Table</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Preposition Lock Table</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">depend / rely / insist</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + ON</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">capable / proud / aware</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + OF</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">responsible / apologize</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + FOR</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">interested / succeed</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">ALWAYS + IN</text></svg>

concepts.title: التعابير المجازية في النصوص
concepts.body: يحمل التعبير الاصطلاحي معنى متفقاً عليه: cut corners التقصير لتوفير الوقت أو المال، وon the fence التردد بين خيارين.
concepts.formula:
تفسير التعبير:
$\text{الموقف العام يفسّر التعبير المجازي}$

examples.title: حرف الجر الثابت مع capable
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Engine designers proved that the compact hydrogen fuel cell is capable ____ powering a bus across steep mountain roads.
أي حرف جر يقترن دائماً بالصفة capable؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: التركيب الإنجليزي الثابت هو capable of + فعل منتهٍ بـ ing أو اسم.

الخطوة 1: تقترن الصفة capable بحرف الجر of دائماً.

✅ التحقق من الحل: of.

examples.title: تفسير تعبير cut corners
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Our chemistry coach warned that lab teams who CUT CORNERS by skipping goggles and scale calibration produce unreliable results.
ما معنى تعبير cut corners في تحذير المشرف؟
options: تجاوز خطوات الدقة والسلامة لاختصار الوقت أو الجهد
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: توضح الجملة نفسه أنهم يتجاوزون إجراءات السلامة والمعايرة اختصاراً، وهذا معنى cut corners.

الخطوة 1: المعنى الاصطلاحي: الإخلال بالجودة اختصاراً للوقت.

✅ التحقق من الحل: تجاوز خطوات الجودة.

examples.explanation:

en.title: Present Perfect, Passive Voice, Conditionals & Relative Clauses
en.summary: Contrast Present Perfect ('since/for/already') vs. Past Simple ('ago/in 2020'), transform Active to Passive voice, build Type 1 & Type 2 conditionals cleanly, and select who/which/whose/where relative connectors.
goals: Use 'since' before starting point (since 2021) and 'for' before elapsed span (for four years).
Use Passive ('be + Past Participle V3') when the object receives the action ('dates are harvested').
Match Conditionals: Type 1 (Real: If + V1 -> will V1) vs. Type 2 (Unreal: If + V2/were -> would V1).

concepts.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple Timeline
concepts.body: Past Simple closes at a finished time ('visited last May'). Present Perfect links past actions to NOW using 'has/have + V3' with 'since' (point) or 'for' (duration).
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 388.1 145" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Present Perfect Span" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:388px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Present Perfect Span</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="129" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Present Perfect Span</text><line x1="36" y1="88" x2="324" y2="88" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="2.2" /><line x1="180" y1="74" x2="180" y2="102" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2" /><text x="52" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Past</text><text x="180" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#0f766e">Now</text><text x="308" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Future</text><line x1="324.0" y1="76" x2="324.0" y2="76" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="4" /><text x="324.0" y="62" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Since 2022 -> Now</text></svg>

concepts.title: Active vs. Passive Voice Matrix
concepts.body: Put the receiver of the action FIRST and conjugate 'be' in the sentence's tense + Past Participle (V3): 'Farmers water palms' -> 'Palms ARE watered daily'.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Passive Voice Forms" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Passive Voice Forms</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Passive Voice Forms</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Present Passive</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Solar panels ARE cleaned weekly</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Past Passive</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">The bridge WAS built in 2019</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Modal Passive</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Helmets MUST BE worn on site</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Key Check</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Subject RECEIVES the verb!</text></svg>

concepts.title: Conditionals & Relative Clauses
concepts.body: Type 1 predicts likely futures (If it rains, we WILL stay). Type 2 imagines unreal presents (If I WERE taller, I WOULD join). Relatives: WHO = person, WHICH = thing, WHOSE = possession, WHERE = place.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Clause Quick Rules" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Clause Quick Rules</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Clause Quick Rules</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">If + Present (V1)</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">... -> WILL + Base</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">If + Past (V2/were)</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">... -> WOULD + Base</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">the engineer ___ design won</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">WHOSE (his/her noun)</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="11.5" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">the lab ___ we tested samples</text><text x="358.5" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">WHERE (at that place)</text></svg>

cheat_sheet.title: Since vs For
cheat_sheet.formula: Count length -> FOR 3 months; Pick date -> SINCE Monday

cheat_sheet.title: Active vs Passive
cheat_sheet.formula: Ask: Can 'the report' WRITE itself? No -> WAS written

cheat_sheet.title: No Will After If
cheat_sheet.formula: Never say 'If it will rain tomorrow'—use Present Simple 'If it rains'

cheat_sheet.title: Whose vs Who
cheat_sheet.formula: Followed directly by a NOUN belonging to person -> WHOSE

traps: Never mix Present Perfect ('have lived') with finished past markers like 'in 2018' or 'yesterday' without 'since'.
Watch out between 'which' vs 'where' for places: 'the library WHICH has 5 floors' (subject/object) vs 'the library WHERE I study' (in/at it).

examples.title: Since vs. For Present Perfect
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Al-Baha's botanical research center has catalogued mountain wildflowers continuously ____ 2019.
Which time preposition introduces the starting year 2019 in Present Perfect?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: 2019 marks a fixed starting date on the timeline rather than a count of years.

Step 1: Start point year 2019 -> since (whereas '5 years' uses 'for').

✅ Quick Check: since.

examples.title: Past Passive Transformation
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
Last semester, four historic Diriyah mud-brick gates ____ carefully by heritage architects.
Choose the passive verb matching plural past subject 'four gates'.
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Check three clues: 'Last semester' (Past), 'four gates' (Plural), and 'by architects' (Passive receiver).

Step 1: Plural + Past Passive -> were + V3 (restored).

✅ Quick Check: were restored.

examples.title: Type 2 Hypothetical Conditional
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
If solar planes carried lighter batteries, cross-desert flights ____ far longer without refueling.
Which result clause pairs with past hypothetical condition 'carried'?
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Type 2 pattern: If + Past Simple ('carried') -> WOULD + base verb.

Step 1: Hypothetical past 'carried' requires modal 'would + last'.

✅ Quick Check: would last.

examples.title: Relative Pronoun Whose vs. Who
examples.question:
Read the walkthrough card.
The marine diver ____ underwater photographs won first prize donated her camera kit to our club.
Choose the relative connector showing 'photographs' belong to 'the diver'.
examples.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Right after the blank sits a noun phrase owned by the diver: 'her underwater photographs'.

Step 1: 'Diver' + 'HER photographs' collapses into 'diver WHOSE photographs'.

✅ Quick Check: whose.

ar.title: المضارع التام والمبني للمجهول والجمل الشرطية وجمل الوصل
ar.summary: التمييز بين المضارع التام والماضي البسيط، صياغة المبني للمجهول، استخدام الجمل الشرطية الأولى والثانية، والربط بضمائر الوصل who/which/whose/where.
goals: التمييز بين since لبداية المدة وfor لطول المدة في المضارع التام.
تطبيق المبني للمجهول (فعل الكينونة + التصريف الثالث) عندما يكون الفاعل غير مذكور أو متأخراً.
المطابقة الزمنية في الشرط الحقيقي (will) والشرط الافتراضي غير الواقعي (would).

concepts.title: المضارع التام مقابل الماضي البسيط
concepts.body: الماضي البسيط ينتهي في زمن محدد مضى (last year)، أما المضارع التام (has/have + V3) فيمتد أثره للحاضر مع since أو for.
concepts.formula:
مفاتيح التام:
$\text{since + نقطة بداية} \mid \text{for + مدة محسوبة}$
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 388.1 145" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Present Perfect Span" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:388px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Present Perfect Span</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="344" height="129" rx="12" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="180" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Present Perfect Span</text><line x1="36" y1="88" x2="324" y2="88" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="2.2" /><line x1="180" y1="74" x2="180" y2="102" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2" /><text x="52" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Past</text><text x="180" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#0f766e">Now</text><text x="308" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#64748b">Future</text><line x1="324.0" y1="76" x2="324.0" y2="76" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="4" /><text x="324.0" y="62" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Since 2022 -> Now</text></svg>

concepts.title: تحويل المبني للمعلوم إلى المجهول
concepts.body: في المبني للمجهول يبدأ الكلام بالمفعول به ثم صيغة من فعل الكينونة في نفس الزمن متبوعاً بالتصريف الثالث V3.
concepts.formula:
معادلة المجهول:
$\text{نائب الفاعل} + \text{be} + \text{التصريف الثالث } V_3$
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Passive Voice Forms" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Passive Voice Forms</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Passive Voice Forms</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Present Passive</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Solar panels ARE cleaned weekly</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Past Passive</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">The bridge WAS built in 2019</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Modal Passive</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Helmets MUST BE worn on site</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Key Check</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Subject RECEIVES the verb!</text></svg>

concepts.title: الشرط وضمائر الوصل
concepts.body: الشرط الأول للواقع المحتمل مع will، والثاني للافتراض التخيلي مع would؛ وضمائر الوصل: who للأشخاص، which للأشياء، whose للملكية، where للمكان.
concepts.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Clause Quick Rules" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Clause Quick Rules</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6" /><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" /><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3" /><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Clause Quick Rules</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">If + Present (V1)</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">... -> WILL + Base</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">If + Past (V2/were)</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">... -> WOULD + Base</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">the engineer ___ design won</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">WHOSE (his/her noun)</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" /><text x="11.5" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">the lab ___ we tested samples</text><text x="358.5" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">WHERE (at that place)</text></svg>

cheat_sheet.title: since مقابل for
cheat_sheet.formula: نقطة بداية محددة تأخذ since، ومقدار زمني محسوب يأخذ for

cheat_sheet.title: اختبار المجهول
cheat_sheet.formula: اسأل: هل يمكن لـ'التقرير' أن يكتب نفسه؟ لا، إذن المبني للمجهول أصح

cheat_sheet.title: حظر will بعد If
cheat_sheet.formula: الجملة الشرطية الأولى تضع المضارع بعد If لا will

cheat_sheet.title: الفرق بين who وwhose
cheat_sheet.formula: إذا تلا الفراغ اسم مملوك للشخص نختار whose لا who

traps: لا تجمع المضارع التام have/has + V3 مع كلمة yesterday أو ago إلا بوجود since.
للمكان: نختار where إذا لم يوجد حرف جر مثل in/at وكان المكان ظرفاً للفعل، أما إذا كان المكان فاعلاً فنختار which.

examples.title: الاختيار بين since وfor
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Al-Baha's botanical research center has catalogued mountain wildflowers continuously ____ 2019.
أي أداة تسبق نقطة البداية 2019 في المضارع التام؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: العام 2019 نقطة بداية محددة للحدث المستمر حتى الآن، فتسبقه since لا for.

الخطوة 1: بما أن بعد الفراغ تاريخ بداية محدد فالجواب since.

✅ التحقق من الحل: since.

examples.title: صياغة المبني للمجهول في الماضي
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
Last semester, four historic Diriyah mud-brick gates ____ carefully by heritage architects.
اختر صيغة المبني للمجهول الصحيحة للفاعل الجمع في الماضي:
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: ثلاث قرائن تحسم الاختيار: جمع (four gates)، وماضٍ (last semester)، ومفعول متأثر بـ (by architects).

الخطوة 1: الجمع في الماضي المجهول يأخذ were + التصريف الثالث.

✅ التحقق من الحل: were restored.
examples.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 186" dir="ltr" role="img" aria-label="Passive Checker" style="display:block;direction:ltr;max-width:100%;width:370px;max-height:280px;margin:14px auto;background:#ffffff;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #cbd5e1"><title>Passive Checker</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="170" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.6"/><rect x="8" y="8" width="354" height="34" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff"/><line x1="8" y1="42" x2="362" y2="42" stroke="#231942" stroke-width="1.3"/><text x="185.0" y="30" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#2563eb">Passive Checker</text><text x="24" y="63" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Time Marker</text><text x="346" y="63" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Last semester (Past)</text><line x1="16" y1="74" x2="354" y2="74" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="95" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Grammatical Subject</text><text x="346" y="95" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">Four gates (Plural receiver)</text><line x1="16" y1="106" x2="354" y2="106" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="127" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Agent Marker</text><text x="346" y="127" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">by heritage architects</text><line x1="16" y1="138" x2="354" y2="138" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1"/><text x="24" y="159" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#231942">Exact Passive Form</text><text x="346" y="159" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#0f766e">were restored</text></svg>

examples.title: الشرط الافتراضي من النوع الثاني
examples.question:
اقرأ المثال المحلول:
If solar planes carried lighter batteries, cross-desert flights ____ far longer without refueling.
أي صيغة جواب شرط تطابق الفعل الماضي التخيلي carried؟
examples.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: الشرط التخيلي (النوع الثاني) يتكون من: If + ماضي بسيط، والنتيجة: would + الفعل المجرد.

الخطوة 1: الفعل الشرطي carried ماضٍ افتراضي، فيقابله would last.

✅ التحقق من الحل: would last.
